milestones.description:
South Gloucestershire Council (SGC) is conducting a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise in relation to its procurement of Temporary Traffic Management services to assist it in developing its requirements and approach.
This engagement is conducted in accordance with Section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023, which permits contracting authorities to engage with the market prior to commencing a procurement procedure.
The purpose of this PME is to:
• Understand market capacity and interest.
• Check and develop procurement requirements.
• Help design procedures, participation conditions and award criteria.
• Identify any potential barriers to participation.
SGC is sharing *DRAFT* Invitation to Tender (ITT) documentation and seeking feedback from the market on the information contained therein.
Participation in this PME is voluntary, but SGC encourages any organisation or group of organisations interested in bidding for this contract to respond to the questions contained within it's 'Preliminary Market Engagement Questionnaire'. Your feedback is valuable in helping us shape a fair, transparent and effective procurement process.
SGC are still finalising their approach and documentation. The responses to its PME Questionnaire will be fed into this process and the finished tender documents are anticipated to be issued shortly after the engagement deadline.
PLEASE NOTE: The e-sender form for the completion of this UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement Notice does not give the option for SGC to specify the closing time for the return of responses. We believe this will display on the notice as 23:59, but the Council asks please that PME Questionnaire responses are returned by 17:00 on Friday 25 September 2026.

tender.title: Unaccompanied Asylum-Seeking Children (UASC) Support Services
tender.description:
The Home Office (the Authority) has a statutory duty under Section 55 of the Borders, Citizenship and Immigration Act 2009 to discharge its immigration and asylum functions having regard to the need to safeguard and promote the welfare of children in the UK. 
This includes Unaccompanied Asylum-Seeking Children (UASC) who arrive in the UK and enter the immigration system without a parent or guardian.
The Support Services for UASC ensure that their immediate needs are met upon arrival in Kent, or elsewhere, prior to entering the care of a local authority. Additionally, there is a need to ensure UASC have access to information and support to help them navigate the asylum process.
The services will operate alongside, and in collaboration with the Authority and a range of other services and Authority suppliers, to enable the effective operation of the system to manage and support UASC. It is recognised that service users may require only one, or a combination of these services at any given time. Therefore, all services areas must be available, but would be delivered on an as-required basis, according to the needs of each individual case.
The core service areas are:
Service Area 1: Delivery of Services at Kent Intake Unit (KIU)
Service Area 2: Delivery of Orientation Sessions

2. Send an 'Expression of Interest' email following the instructions:
a. Email to: asylumsupportprocurementteam@homeoffice.gov.uk
b. Email subject: Expression of Interest - UASC - NDA Request - (DUNS number)
3. The email must include the following:
a. Supplier name (as on Companies House)
b. DUNS number
c. Jaggaer Account ID
d. Contact person - Name, job title, email address, contact number
4. The Supplier will then be asked to complete the NDA and return this document back to the Authority for countersignature. This shall be done via the Jaggaer Portal NDA event.
5. Suppliers whose NDAs have been countersigned will be granted access to the Invitation to Tender Event in Jaggaer

tender.description:
The Council is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced Contractor to provide a responsive and flexible service for the supply, delivery and installation of carpeting and associated flooring materials within accommodation allocated to homeless households throughout the Wychavon district. 
Indicative Demand and Property Requirements:
The information below is provided for guidance only and is based on carpeting requests received between November 2025 and June 2026. It is intended to assist Tenderers in understanding the typical demand for the Services and the nature of the carpeting requirements. The Council does not guarantee any minimum volume of work under this Contract.
•	During the period November 2025 to June 2026, the Council received 61 carpet referrals.
•	Based on this historical data, this equates to approximately 90 referrals per annum.
•	This annual figure is provided for indicative purposes only and should not be regarded as a guarantee of future demand.
•	For single-person households, carpeting is typically provided to the living room and one bedroom.
•	For two-bedroom properties, carpeting is typically provided to the living room and one child's bedroom.
•	For three-bedroom properties, carpeting is typically provided to the living room and two children's bedrooms.
•	For four-bedroom properties, carpeting is typically provided to the living room and three children's bedrooms.
Please see the procurement documents for further information.

tender.title: End User Workspace and Hosting
tender.description:
The End User Workspace & Hosting procurement event was to secure a single supplier to deliver both End User Workspace (EUW) and Hosting services under a single contract. The Services had to be ITIL-aligned and delivered using the Council's own ServiceNow ITSM platform, with contract aims of improving service delivery, reducing complexity, and enhance user experience through integrated support.
Key requirements of scope:
• Service Desk - Single point of contact for all ICT issues, with a focus on first-contact resolution and self-service enablement.
• Incident Management - Rapid restoration of normal service with clear ownership and root cause analysis.
• Problem Management - Identification and elimination of root causes to reduce incident recurrence.
• Change Enablement - Safe, timely implementation of changes with strong governance, TAB and CAB participation.
• Service Request Management - Efficient fulfilment of user requests via a structured service catalogue.
• Service Configuration & Asset Management - Accurate tracking of assets and configuration items using ServiceNow CMDB.
• Release & Deployment Management - Controlled rollout of new
software and updates, including packaging and testing.
• Availability & Capacity Management - Ensuring services meet
performance and uptime targets, with proactive planning.
• Monitoring & Event Management - Real-time monitoring and alerting to detect and respond to issues before they impact users.
• Security Management - ISO27001-compliant controls, vulnerability management, and incident response.
• Service Continuity Management - Disaster recovery planning and testing to ensure resilience.
• Knowledge Management - Centralised, structured knowledge base to support selfservice and efficient resolution.
• Supplier & Risk Management - Collaboration across multiple suppliers with shared risk registers and joint governance.
• Continual Improvement - Ongoing service enhancements tracked via a formal improvement plan and CMMI assessments.
• Project & Portfolio Management - Support for operational,
enhancement, and strategic projects with defined governance
End User Workspace (EUW):
• Service Desk (first-line support, triage, escalation, and resolution).
• Deskside Support (field engineering across 66 sites).
• Second Line Support (technical escalation, patching, anti-virus and infrastructure support
• Device lifecycle management (builds, refresh, repairs).
• Microsoft 365 and Windows 11 environment support.
• Knowledge management and training provision.
Service Management Expectations
• Operate within a SIAM model with strong collaboration across
suppliers.
• Use of ServiceNow for all ITSM functions (incident, problem, change, asset, etc.).
• Monthly and annual reporting, SLA/KPI tracking, and continual
improvement.
• Supplier must achieve CMMI Level 3 within 6 months.
The contract is over 7 years (including extensions), with published contract value of £13,800,000 (inclusive of VAT)

tender.title: Merchant Acquiring Services
tender.description:
Merchant Acquiring is an essential contract from a financial perspective as it is necessary to enable residents and customers to pay the council by debit and credit card, over £100m a year is collected by the council using this contract.
This service is a key part of the council’s support systems, and essential for the council to be able to collect payments by card as people expect in 2026. 
The contract helps enable the goals set out in the Customer Access Strategy to strive to make the online customer journey accessible, user-friendly and straightforward, as customers expect to be able to pay for services online using their cards.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
This is a complex contract to re-procure, involving both a complex, technical procurement, and multiple council departments with differing specifications. If awarded to a different supplier then there is significant work to transition several of the council’s financial systems to use the new supplier which would not be possible for technical and operational reasons before the existing contract expires. The Council cannot risk the disruption to this service as this would impact income collection via e-commerce, online or telephone payments from residents and customers.
Therefore, Officers intend to use this time in an effective way to plan a new procurement exercise and procure compliantly a suitably experienced supplier to deliver and support the transition to a possible new supplier of merchant acquiring services.

Brief Description of Requirement
Phase 1
The objective of phase 1 is to assess the safety and risk considerations for deployment of up to 800 W AC mains output plug-in batteries in the UK context with acceptable electrical and fire safety risk. The study will inform technical standards adaptations and assess the feasibility of safe, plug-in batteries for UK domestic use. 
A relevant set of installation configurations will need to be considered in scope of the fire and electrical safety tests and will be finalised as part of the test protocol development for the study, in consultation with relevant stakeholders. These installation configurations may include individual plug-in batteries, plug-in battery DC-coupled to plug-in solar with a single hybrid inverter, multiple plug-in batteries DC-coupled in series, and multiple plug-in batteries DC-coupled in parallel. An illustrative set of installation configurations that might be expected to be considered by the supplier when developing the test protocol are provided below, noting that the tests should focus on the standalone plug-in battery products and/or the plug-in battery to plug-in solar interface rather than the wider domestic environment in which they are located.

tender.description:
As part of our ongoing efforts to support the co-op and community-led housing sector, we have procured a managing agent for Frameworks designed to deliver flexible, technology-enabled repairs, maintenance, consultancy and major works services to us and other similar organisations.
Our managing agent, Plentific, is a UK-based property technology company that will use its platform to manage this Framework, ensuring Contracting Authorities are able to access the services offered by Suppliers admitted to the Framework.
Services delivered by this Framework will be to domestic and commercial properties. Domestic properties will typically consist of a mixture of domestic housing sites but not limited to bungalows, blocks of flats, and co-operative housing schemes and any other building owned and/or managed by our Framework contracting agent. Commercial properties will include but not be limited to business units, office buildings and community centres.
The Framework comprises four lots, with Contracting Authorities being able to source services from Suppliers by becoming users of the Plentific platform.
Contracts described in this Notice are SOLELY FOR LOT 1. Tender Notices for lots 2, 3 and 4 are estimated to be published from December 2027.
Suppliers will be able to apply for admission to the framework at regular intervals. Contracting Authorities will be able to appoint Suppliers through direct award or mini-competition tender process.
No framework has been previously awarded under the Open Framework.

tender.title: Provision of Security Services for the Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
tender.description: The buyer is seeking proposals for the security, guarding and operational service at the Supreme Court of the United Kingdom (UKSC). The service is in place to ensure the safety of Justices, staff, contractors, visitors, and the physical site itself, as well as ensuring the work of the Court, both at its main site and any other location where the work or activities of the Court take place, are done safely and securely.

lots.description:
The UKSC is the United Kingdom's highest court of appeal. It hears appeals on arguable points of law of general public importance, concentrating on cases of the greatest significance. The UKSC is the final court of appeal for all United Kingdom civil cases, and criminal cases from England, Wales and Northern Ireland and (in certain cases) Scotland. The Court plays an important role in the development of UK law. The impact of UKSC decisions extends far beyond the parties involved in any given case, helping to shape our society. Its judgments directly affect everyday lives.
The requirement of this contract is for guarding of the UKSC in Parliament Square for an initial period of three years from the commencement of service, and extendable at the discretion of the UKSC for a further two-year period of up to one year each (bringing the total maximum possible term of the contract up to five years).
The UKSC is located on Parliament Square and is therefore recognised to be within the Government Secure Zone. The Supplier will need to deploy an appropriate number of security officers, with relevant training and qualifications, to control access and guarding on a 24-hour basis, throughout the contract period to prevent unauthorised access to the premises or any harm to the premises, persons or assets therein.
The UKSC is both a non -ministerial government department and a fully operational court and educational destination for the Rule of Law. The Supplier has to ensure that officers and others working on this contract meet the operational and statutory requirements required which include, but are not limited to, the requirements of the SIA and the Security Officer requirements as set out in the Constitutional Reform Act 2025.
The site is open to the public Monday through to Friday between the hours of 08:30 and 17:30, but the building is also used for corporate and charitable events out of hours, where officers will be required to be on site.

tender.title: Residential and Nursing Care Homes for Adults - Framework Agreement
tender.description:
Nottinghamshire County Council is procuring a Framework Agreement for the provision of residential and/or nursing care home services for adults. The Council intends to appoint multiple successful bidders as Providers under the Framework.
The Framework will support individuals whose primary support needs include learning disabilities, autism, mental health needs, physical disabilities, brain injuries and sensory impairments. Services may include standard placements, short breaks, emergency placements, forensic provision and exceptional and highly specialist care arrangements.
The service is primarily for adults. The Council may also use the Framework to commission provision for young people aged 16 or 17, provided that the relevant home satisfies all applicable registration, policy and regulatory requirements, including those of the Care Quality Commission and/or Ofsted.
For older adults, typically those aged 65 and over, the Council will ordinarily commission residential provision through alternative contracts that the Council has developed specifically for residential care for older adults. It is anticipated that this Framework will only be used for people aged 65 years and over in exceptional circumstances where suitable provision cannot be identified via the alternative contracts.
Most placements are expected to be within the seven districts of Nottinghamshire. However, the Council may commission placements outside of Nottinghamshire where required.
Bidders are advised that, following the UK Government's publication of the English Devolution White Paper in December 2024, a programme of Local Government Reorganisation ("LGR") is underway which may affect the governance, boundaries and/or legal status of the Council during the term of any Framework or Call-Off Contract entered pursuant to this procurement. As a consequence of LGR, any Framework or Call-Off Contract may be required to be transferred, assigned or novated (in whole or in part) to one or more successor authorities or other public bodies established as part of LGR, in accordance with applicable legislation.
The Council intends to establish this Framework for an initial term of 6 years, with the option to extend for up to two further periods of 24 months (6+2+2). The maximum potential duration of the Framework is therefore 10 years.
Appointment to the Framework does not guarantee a Provider any volume of placements or minimum level of expenditure.
The Council reserves the right, at its discretion, to advertise one or more further opportunities to admit additional Providers to the Framework. No dates have been set for any such opportunities. Any future opportunity will be separately advertised and conducted in accordance with the applicable procurement requirements. A bidder that is unsuccessful in this procurement may submit a new tender in response to any future advertised opportunity but a bidder that has been successful will not need to re-apply. For the avoidance of doubt this Framework is not an Open Framework within the meaning of the Procurement Act 2023.
Full details of the requirements are set out in the procurement documents.

frameworkAgreement.description:
For the Framework Agreement all bidders meeting the minimum quality threshold of 60% and assessed as meeting the Conditions of Participation will be selected for award.
Awards of Call-Off Contracts under the Framework will be made using one of the following approaches:
•  Direct Award; or
•  Further Competition.
Circumstances for Direct Awards
A Direct Award may be made in any of the following circumstances, subject to the requirements set out in Schedule 2 of the Framework:
a) Emergency Placement
Where the Council has fewer than 72 hours to secure a placement because of an immediate risk or urgent need. Emergency Placements are exceptional and time-limited and must not be used for routine or planned placements. The award of Emergency Placements will be facilitated by the Service Profile Summary provided by each bidder when they join the Framework which includes, but is not limited to, details of 'core costs' for each care home.
b) Transfer of an Existing Placement
Where a Service User is already in an established placement commissioned by an Integrated Care Board, another commissioning body or another local authority, and responsibility for commissioning the placement transfers to the Council.
This route may only be used where it would not be proportionate or appropriate to undertake a Further Competition and it would not be in the Service User's best interests to move or re-procure the placement.
c) Individual Service User Choice
Where a Service User has expressed a clear and informed preference for a specific Provider and the Council considers it appropriate to support that preference.
This route may only be used where the Council is satisfied that the Provider can meet the Service User's assessed needs and the applicable requirements of Schedule 2.
All Direct Awards must be appropriately justified and approved and are subject to the due diligence, quality, pricing, value-for-money and contracting requirements set out in Schedule 2 of the Framework.
Circumstances for further competitions
A Further Competition may be undertaken where:
•	A planned placement is required
•	More than 72 hours is available to secure the placement
•	Following the completion of an emergency placement period, ongoing support is required
•	There is a requirement for a block arrangement for the placement of more than one individual
The evaluation criteria will be based on criteria defined at the Further Competition ITT stage.
Quality award criteria may vary in weighting between 25% and 100%.
Price award criteria may vary in weighting between 0% and 75%.
The Council reserves the right, at its discretion, to advertise one or more further opportunities to admit additional Providers to the Framework. No dates have been set for any such opportunities. Any future opportunity will be separately advertised and conducted in accordance with the applicable procurement requirements. A bidder that is unsuccessful in this procurement may submit a new tender in response to any future advertised opportunity but a bidder that has been successful will not need to re-apply. For the avoidance of doubt this Framework is not an Open Framework within the meaning of the Procurement Act 2023.

tender.title: Crisis and Resilience Fund Hub Delivery
tender.description:
The Department for Work and Pensions introduced the Crisis and Resilience Fund from 1 April 2026. The Fund provides local authorities with funding to support households experiencing financial hardship or an unexpected financial shock and to help residents build longer-term financial resilience. Southwark Council is developing a hub-and-spoke model to support the delivery of the Resilience Services and Community Coordination elements of the Fund. 
The Council is considering commissioning a Hub Delivery Organisation (HDO) to provide a central and accessible route into financial-resilience support for Southwark residents. The Council will retain responsibility for administering Council-managed crisis and housing-related payments, determining eligibility, making formal decisions on applications for financial assistance and submitting formal management-information returns to the Department for Work and Pensions. 
Further information about the emerging HDO service model, the areas being considered, local delivery and accessibility, case management, reporting, and the indicative contract value and duration is set out in the accompanying Draft Service Specification. 
The final scope and delivery model have not been determined. Therefore, the Council is carry out a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) where respondents are invited to use the information provided via the portal, see engagement process description further down in this notice. Respondents are requested to use both documents when completing the questionnaire and should clearly state any assumptions made in their responses.

tender.title: CS6100 Voluntary and Community Sector Coordinator Services
tender.description:
London Borough of Tower Hamlets is committed to developing a thriving Voluntary and Community Sector (VCS) sector to assist with shaping its strategic vision and supporting the delivery of key priorities for children, young people and families. The local VCS sector is a valuable partner, and the Council invests significantly in developing and commissioning via the VCS a broad range of services to support children, young people and families that live or have links to the borough.
To support the delivery of the children and young people's strategy, the Council is seeking a Provider that can ensure the continued delivery of the VCS Coordinator Service. The Service will play a key enabling role in ensuring the Council's continued partnership work with voluntary and community sector organisations and the wider third sector, within the borough and beyond, with a specific focus on those organisations who work in the children and young people's sector.
The overall aim behind the Service is to develop stronger, more engaged and sustainable partnerships with a wider range of partners, drawing on the extensive experience and expertise that voluntary and community sector organisations have in responding to the needs, and enriching the lives, of children, young people and families in Tower Hamlets.

Gloucestershire ICB and Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG) ICB are merging to form a single integrated body in April 2027. Both organisations currently rely on external providers for the delivery of their IT services. A new, unified service model is required; one that supports the merged organisation from day one, is commercially sustainable, and is capable of evolving as the ICS matures.
Six principles shape the design of the future service:
1. Cloud-first and 'secure by design'. All new and renewed services will be cloud-based wherever possible. On-premises infrastructure will be exited as part of transition. This is both a strategic choice and a compliance requirement under the Government Cloud First Policy and Technology Code of Practice.
2. Outcome-focused. The service is defined by what it must deliver, not how it must be delivered. The supplier is expected to bring expertise, innovation and accountability for outcomes, not simply execute a prescriptive technical specification.
3. Single point of accountability. The preferred model is a single managed service provider with end-to-end accountability for operational delivery. This avoids the fragmentation and unclear ownership that characterises the current multi-supplier landscape and reduces the management overhead on the ICB digital team.
4. Lean governance. The ICB digital team will provide strategic oversight, roadmap ownership and supplier governance. It will not carry operational delivery responsibilities. This reflects the lean, strategically focused character of the merged organisation and the direction set by the Model ICB Blueprint.
5. Interoperable by design. The service must integrate cleanly with nationally contracted NHS platforms, in particular NHS.net Connect, the Health and Social Care Network (HSCN) and NHS Secure Boundary Service, as well as local platforms, such as the Gloucestershire ICS WAN and into UHBW and Crown Datacentres in Corsham. Service interfaces with these platforms should be clearly defined before the procurement specification is finalised.
6. Sustainable. The ICB's carbon neutral commitments should be reflected in technology choices, including energy-efficient end-user devices, PoE-powered monitors and cloud-based infrastructure in preference to on-premises data centre equipment.
The following service stacks are in scope for the new managed service, reflecting services currently provided across both incumbents, consolidated and extended to support the merged organisation:
- Service desk. The primary user-facing support channel, available 08:00-18:00 Monday to Friday. 
- Desktop support. Onsite presence at both sites as and when required, including end-user support, moves, adds and changes to desktop arrangements, MFD, Audio Visual equipment, and Teams Room management. The onsite support model must include provision for routine physical tasks including WFH equipment management, peripheral replacement, cable and hardware swap-outs, and stock management.
- End-user compute. Device lifecycle management including provisioning, refresh (five-year target cycle), configuration, and secure disposal.
- Telephony and unified communications. Microsoft Teams Phone as the unified platform for the merged ICB.
- Print. Cloud-managed secure print at both sites.
- Meeting rooms. Physical teams Room management and audio-visual support at 2 locations with 15 meeting rooms at one and at Shire Hall, Gloucester and 9 at the second location. 
- Asset management. Asset tagging, recording, and lifecycle tracking for all ICB-owned IT equipment. 
- Supplier and procurement management. The supplier will assume management of all ongoing third-party technology relationships and will procure all IT equipment and recurring support contracts on behalf of the ICB. Licence management across the estate is required.
- DSPT support. The supplier is expected to provide the ICB with the technical evidence and assurance data required to support annual DSPT submission, including patch management records, asset inventory, access control logs and incident reports.
- Project, change and architecture. The supplier will own project and change management, problem management, and architecture design.
- Digital signatures. Digital signature capability is required as part of the new service.
Full details are provided in the service specification.
The total maximum contract value for the initial 3-year Contract is £1,920,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable). 
At the end of the initial contract term the Commissioner will have two, separate, consecutive one-year extension option periods that can be exercised at the discretion of the Commissioner, giving a maximum possible contract value of £2,700,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable) over 5 years if the full contract term is fulfilled.
The Commissioner is of the view that TUPE does not apply to this service.
The Contracting Authority reserves the right to use the Direct Award procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 for any subsequent extensions or new contracts for similar requirements.
The new contract will commence on 1st April 2027, although implementation of the services will start during January 2026.

releases.description:
In reaching its decision, the Council considered all five key criteria under the Provider Selection Regime. Particular emphasis was placed on Quality and Innovation, Value, and Integration, Collaboration and Service Sustainability, as these criteria were considered most relevant in assessing whether the existing provider is likely to continue delivering a high-quality, effective and sustainable occupational physiotherapy service throughout the proposed contract term. Improving Access, Reducing Health Inequalities and Facilitating Choice, and Social Value were also considered as part of the overall assessment. Whilst these criteria remained important, certain aspects were less directly applicable given that the service is provided exclusively to Council employees rather than the wider population.
The assessment found that the existing provider consistently meets contractual requirements and performance expectations, with extensive evidence demonstrating positive employee outcomes, service quality, and continuous improvement. The provider has established effective working relationships with Human Resources, managers and Employees, as well as complementing the Council's existing Occupational Health, Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) and wider wellbeing provision. Through early intervention, treatment, rehabilitation and workplace advice, it forms an integral part of the Council's preventative approach to workforce health and wellbeing, helping employees access the right support at the right time. No significant performance concerns, complaints or service delivery issues were identified.
The Council also concluded that the service continues to provide strong value for money when considering both cost and wider organisational benefits. Evidence considered included the service's contribution to reducing the financial burden associated with ill-health and musculoskeletal absence, benchmarking against comparable physiotherapy services provided by other local authorities and public sector organisations, and a desktop review of local market and wider UK physiotherapy market data.
The assessment also considered the costs and benefits of maintaining the existing arrangement over the proposed contract term, including the avoidance of implementation and mobilisation costs, continuity of service delivery, reduction of service disruption risks, preservation of employee satisfaction, and cost certainty over the life of the contract. Collectively, this evidence demonstrated that the existing provider continues to deliver a cost-effective service that supports positive workforce outcomes and represents value for money.
Having considered the evidence against all five key criteria, the Council concluded that the existing provider continues to satisfy the current contract, is likely to satisfy the proposed contract to a sufficient standard, and that the proposed contracting arrangements are not changing considerably. The Relevant Authority therefore intends to award the contract to the existing provider under Direct Award Process C.
Award Decision-Making Body: Cabinet, Wolverhampton City Council.
All officers involved in the assessment and recommendation process completed the required conflict of interest declarations. No actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest were identified, and therefore no mitigation actions were required.

The standstill period requirements, including for the reviewing of decisions, are detailed in Regulations 12 and 14(3). Provision for independent expert advice is set out in Regulation 23.
Providers may make a representation to the relevant authority within the first eight working days (14 September 2026 - 23 September 2026) following the start of the standstill period (i.e., eight working days starting with the first working day following the day after the intention to award notice has been published). Providers cannot submit a representation after that period, even if the standstill period has been extended in response to a representation from another provider.
Any provider wishing to make representations in accordance with Regulation 12 of the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 should submit them in writing to Corporate.Procurement@wolverhampton.gov.uk before the end of the standstill period.
Relevant authorities are only obliged to respond to representations that meet all the following conditions:
* the representation comes from a provider that might otherwise have been a provider of the services to which the contract relates
* the provider is aggrieved by the decision of the Council
* the provider believes that the Council has failed to apply the regime correctly and is able to set out reasonable grounds to support its belief
* the representation is submitted in writing (which includes electronically) to the Council within eight working days of the start of the standstill period.
If a provider remains unsatisfied about the response given by the Council to their representations, then that provider may seek the involvement of the Independent Patient Choice and Procurement Panel. 
If a provider wishes to request the panel to consider their representation further, then they must submit their request through the panel's website (find address below) within five working days of receiving the relevant authority's decision following the relevant authority's review of their representation.
https://www.england.nhs.uk/commissioning/how-commissioning-is-changing/nhs-provider-selection-regime/independent-patient-choice-and-procurement-panel/

tender.title: Mental Health Day Opportunities Service - Market Engagement Event | Remote
tender.description:
The Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC), working in partnership with Westminster City Council (WCC), is undertaking a market engagement exercise to gather information regarding premises that may be suitable for the delivery of the proposed Adult Social Care Mental Health Day Opportunities model.
The proposed service model is expected to commence during Spring/Summer 2027 and is currently being developed following earlier market engagement activity. The model is anticipated to comprise three locality-based hubs across the borough:
(i)North Hub
(ii)South Hub
(iii)Cultural Hub (located in the north of the borough)
These hubs will provide accommodation to support staff delivery, key working, care coordination, group activities and service user engagement. The service model will also utilise community assets across the borough, including community venues, libraries, green spaces and other suitable facilities to support flexible delivery within local neighbourhoods.
Through this engagement, the Council wishes to better understand:
(i)The availability of suitable premises within the borough.
(ii)Capacity, accessibility and physical characteristics of available spaces.
(iii)Potential leasing, licensing or partnership arrangements.
(iv)Opportunities to support community-based mental health day opportunities from existing assets.
(v)Indicative costs, constraints and considerations relating to premises provision.
Interested organisations, landlords, community organisations, faith groups, charities, social enterprises, property managers and other relevant stakeholders are invited to complete a short questionnaire.
Information gathered will be used to inform future service design, commissioning and procurement planning. Participation in this engagement exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any future procurement process, nor does it constitute a call for competition.
The Council reserves the right to amend its requirements and procurement strategy following completion of this engagement activity.

tender.title: ORT 0210 - Long-Term Contract for the Through-Life End-To-End Support of the Stopped Vehicle Detection Service.
tender.description:
National Highways is planning a future procurement for the provision of a long-term Through-Life Support Contract for its Stopped Vehicle Detection (SVD) Service across England’s Strategic Road Network (SRN). Covering over 4,500 miles of motorways and major A roads, the SRN is a vital component of the UK’s transport infrastructure, carrying a third of all traffic and two-thirds of freight.
The requirement is expected to support approximately 27 operational SVD schemes across 6-Regions of the SRN. Where each SVD scheme is monitored by a nominated Regional Operations Centre (ROC).
The service supports the safe operation of All Lane Running sections of motorway through the provision and maintenance of SVD technology and associated support services.
The installed SVD estate comprises approximately 1,310 endpoint devices. The future contract requires support, maintenance, both reactive and cyclical, and improvement of the SVD application and associated operational systems. Telecommunications services provided through the National Roads Telecommunications Service (NRTS) are currently anticipated to remain outside the scope of the procurement.
This Pipeline Notice is intended to provide advance visibility of a potential future procurement and to assist supplier market awareness and planning.

tender.title: Peatland ACTION FW02 Field Ecologists Framework
tender.description:
NatureScot work to improve our natural environment in Scotland and inspire everyone to care more about it. We work to ensure that all nature in Scotland - our key habitats and landscapes, all our green space and our native species - are maintained, enhanced and bring us benefits. Our priority is a nature-rich future for Scotland and an effective response to the climate emergency.
Peatland ACTION funding - from Scottish Government - primarily supports on-the-ground peatland restoration activities and is open for applications from eligible land managers who have peatlands that would benefit from restoration. There are no geographical restrictions or target areas for Peatland ACTION funding. Peatlands are an iconic part of the Scottish landscape and have many benefits for people and nature. Healthy peatlands provide important ecosystem services including storing and sequestering carbon, supporting unique and specialised biodiversity, improving downstream water quality, and regulating water flow to provide natural flood management. In contrast, damage to peatlands reduces or reverses these benefits. For example, degraded peatlands release stored carbon and are a major global source of greenhouse gas emissions.
Peatland ACTION is led and funded by Scottish Government and delivered in partnership with NatureScot, Cairngorms National Park Authority, Loch Lomond & the Trossachs National Park Authority, Forestry and Land Scotland, and Scottish Water.
Since 2012, Peatland ACTION has set over 66,000 hectares of degraded peatland on the road to recovery, but this effort needs to accelerate rapidly in the coming years to help address the twin crises of the climate emergency and biodiversity loss.
The appointed Field Ecologists will work with the Peatland ACTION Technical Team and Project Officers located across Scotland to help support species and ecological survey requirements for Peatland ACTION restoration sites.

lots.description:
The primary role for the appointed Field Ecologists will be to carry out protected species surveys on request, which may include surveys for breeding birds (including Schedule 1 species), raptor roosts, mammals, freshwater pearl mussel, reptiles, or plants.
Field Ecologists must be suitably skilled and experienced in carrying out a range of species surveys of this nature. Surveys conducted prior to peatland restoration work commencing on site will be used to plan the restoration work and ensure all project personnel (agents, contractors / workers) are aware of the presence of any protected species on site and any mitigation and licensing requirements.
Surveys conducted during restoration works will also be used to provide continued ecological support to project personnel, including mitigation requirements, safe working distances/buffer zones, preparation of species protection plans and may include giving toolbox talks. Additional information: Scotland Excel is acting on behalf of NatureScot in the execution of this tender but will not be party to the contract or the management of the contract throughout its lifetime.

tender.title: PROVISION OF GENERAL SUPPORTED LIVING SERVICES
tender.description:
Bridgend County Borough Council are looking to recommission its General Supported Living services which will include care and support funded by both Adult Social Care and the Housing Support Grant. 
The Council intends to recommission the 7 Lots under this contract where support is provided to individuals living in General Supported Living services across the Bridgend County Borough. These services will be provided by high-quality Providers who can demonstrate their experience of delivering supported living services. These 7 Lots will be awarded as separate Contracts. 
Providers will be required to work with the Council to implement sustainable and flexible models of support that enable Individuals to become active members of their local communities. Delivering a ‘locality’ model will continue to enable Providers to flexibly respond to the needs of the individuals they support as and where they arise, utilise resources efficiently, and support collaborative working with the broader community. The service must be available 24 hours a day, 365 days per year in line with the assessed needs of Individuals.
The procurement process will be conducted in a single stage.
Prospective providers will be able to bid for as many of the lots as they wish, however the Council will be looking to secure a mixed market where each provider will be limited to being awarded a maximum of two Lot areas. Each Lot’s requirements will be different and so suits a range of Providers.
Benchmark data indicates that the service in current schemes totals 8979 hours of support per week delivered to 89 Individuals living in 34 housing units. Please note this is for information purposes only and further Local Area Service details will be provided to the successful providers following the conclusion and award of the Lot contracts. 
The contract agreement duration will be for an initial 4 years with additional, discretional contract extension periods for an addition up to a further 4 years. It will remain the council’s decision as to if and how any contract extension is implemented.

awardCriteria.description:
Lot Allocation
The Council intends to recommission the 7 Lots under this contract where support is provided to individuals living in General Supported Living services across the Bridgend County Borough. These services will be provided by high-quality Providers who can demonstrate their experience of delivering supported living services. These 7 Lots will be awarded as separate Contracts. 
Prospective providers will be able to bid for as many of the lots as they wish. However, the Council will be looking to secure a mixed market where each provider will be limited to being awarded a maximum of two Lot areas. Each Lot’s requirements will be different and so suits a range of Providers.
Lot Allocation Rationale & Criteria:
First Tiebreak Criteria: 
The lot will be awarded to the bidder with the highest score in the Quality/Technical evaluation.
Second Tiebreaker Criteria:
If scores are tied, the lot will be awarded to the bidder with the highest score in the highest-weighted Lot Specific Question.
In the event that a single provider submits the Most Advantageous Tender (MAT) for more than two lots, the Council will apply an objective mechanism (Suppliers Stated Preference) to determine contract allocation. 
Supplier’s Stated Preference
Bidders must state their order of preference for the lots using the Lot Preference Form, located within the qualification envelope of the Core Requirements itt_127077. If a bidder ranks first in more than two lots, they will be awarded the two lots for which they indicated the highest preference. The remaining lot(s) will be awarded to the next highest-scoring bidder for those specific lots.

tender.title: CPT_26_03 IT Service management (ITSM)
tender.description:
The National Audit Office (NAO) is the UK's independent public spending watchdog. It supports Parliament in holding government to account and helps improve public services through high quality audit and assurance work.
The NAO sought to appoint an experienced supplier to provide an enterprise-grade IT Service Management (ITSM) solution and associated support services for internal users across the organisation.
The requirement included the provision, implementation, configuration, and ongoing support of an ITSM platform capable of supporting core ITSM processes, including incident management, service requests, change management, asset and configuration management, workflow automation, reporting, and governance. The solution is required to be scalable, configurable, and proportionate to the NAO's operational needs, and capable of supporting multiple internal functional areas.
The procurement sought a supplier capable of delivering a controlled transition from the incumbent system, including secure data migration, integration with the NAO's Microsoft-based digital estate, and service readiness activities, with minimal disruption to business operations. The solution is required to provide an intuitive user experience, configurable workflows, and accessible reporting, without reliance on complex development or ongoing external consultancy.
The requirement also included robust ongoing platform support, including routine updates, security maintenance and patching, and effective vulnerability management and remediation. This includes the ability to identify, assess, track, prioritise, and remediate security vulnerabilities affecting the ITSM platform and its components, supported by appropriate controls, governance, and reporting.
The successful supplier is required to provide assurance that vulnerabilities are managed in line with recognised industry good practice and the NAO's information security and risk management requirements.
In addition, the procurement sought a supplier able to demonstrate a sustainable product roadmap and ongoing service support model to ensure long-term service continuity, platform resilience, and alignment with the NAO's future operational and digital requirements.
The contract will commence on Monday 2 November 2026 and includes an initial six-month mobilisation and implementation period, with service go-live anticipated from Tuesday 1 June 2027.
The initial contract term is three (3) years until Friday 31 May 2030, with options to extend for up to two further periods of twelve (12) months, up to a maximum contract end date of Monday 31 May 2032.
The contract has been awarded with a maximum value of up to £1.8 million inclusive of VAT over the full potential five-year term.

renewal.description: The NAO reserves the right to extend the Contract by up to two (2) additional periods of twelve (12) months each, up to a maximum end date of Monday 31st May 2032.

tender.description:
Bath & North East Somerset Council is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced contractor led team to test, investigate, appraise and develop a range of deliverable options for the replacement of the Pulteney Radial Gate on the river Avon in the centre of Bath.
A range of options are being considered, including 1) a Hydro-Station 2a) Extend the existing Horseshoe Weir 2b) Create a Stepped Weir within the existing channel 3) Infill the existing channel to create new public realm 4a) Own & Operate the Gate, 4b) Do Minimum to the Asset.
Each option will need to be assessed against relevant access, logistics and construction constraints.
The appointment will include the review and validation of existing project information;  coordination and execution of intrusive and investigative survey workstreams; assessment of site access, interfaces, constraints and stakeholder considerations; and comparative appraisal of the options and associated logistics scenarios. The appointed contractor will be expected to provide advice on buildability, temporary works, programme, cost, risk, Principal Designer/CDM matters and whole-life implications.
The commission is intended to establish a well evidenced technical, commercial and construction basis for the project, in order to support the Outline Business Case at P3M Stage 2.
This commission is separate to any future decision to progress to detailed design, statutory approvals or main works procurement.
The output will be a series of in-depth evidenced based appraisal reports with a final composite report and recommendation to support Outline Business Case decision-making and any future route-to-market strategy for the Main Works.

tender.title: NLP Condition Survey Programme
tender.description:
North Lanarkshire Properties (NLP) has a requirement to update its asset management register in respect of the condition of its property estate to ensure compliance with its statutory and legal obligations and to inform a multiyear investment strategy. The resulting dataset will form the foundation of NLP's future asset management, lifecycle investment, maintenance planning and portfolio optimisation activities. NLP manages a portfolio of approximately 990 assets. The current condition survey programme is anticipated to cover approximately 672 operational property assets, excluding ground lease assets and other property categories outside the scope of this procurement. Information is required on the following split:
- 4 Business Centres
- 28 Offices
- 233 Retail
- 402 Industrial
- 5 Miscellaneous
- 672 Total
The procurement is for the appointment of suitably qualified and experienced building surveyor (a “Contractor”) to carry out condition surveys across a number of properties within the NLP portfolio.
The aim of the resulting Agreement is to obtain by means of visual inspection consistent, accurate and actionable information regarding the physical condition, statutory compliance, risks, and investment needs of the defined buildings within the estate. Applying the findings to inform a data driven investment strategy to maximise portfolio value. The objectives are to:
- Establish the current physical condition of each property asset defined.
- Identify defects, risks, and compliance issues.
- Provide an assessment of each asset’s life.
- Provide prioritised maintenance actions. Year 1-5 with year 1 being the faults in most urgent need of attention.
- Provide costs as a basis for estimating and to identify the level of funding required for future capital and revenue expenditure.
- Provide sufficient information to allow a maintenance programme to be developed over a planned period that will support operational planning and asset management decision making
- Deliver the condition survey in accordance with the following mandatory professional standards:
a. RICS Building Surveying Standards & Guidance
b. RICS Surveying Safely
c. RICS New Rules of Measurement (NRM) for cost estimation
d. PFI Asset Condition Playbook (2025) – survey methodology and reporting guidance
e. General Implementation Guidance (2025) for asset condition hand back surveys
f. Centre of Best Practice (CoBP) specification (where applicable)
The purpose of the commission is to provide portfolio-wide condition intelligence to support NLP asset management and investment decisions through Level 1 visual, non-intrusive surveys.

lots.description:
Geographical programme approach to be taken commencing with largest area; undertaking site visits to each property asset included in the programme (exc ground lease assets) as per tender documentation.
Elements in scope
- Contractor to deliver Condition Survey Level 1 visual non-intrusive inspections including review of available compliance documentation and identification of visible compliance concerns across external, internal, M&E elements, plus compliance observations.
- ID issues that relate to building energy performance and carbon emissions e.g. visible inefficiencies, highlighting old/inefficient systems, flagging fabric defects and heat loss risks.
- Undertake site visits, during normal opening hours, to each property asset included in the programme.
Conduct non-destructive inspection unless otherwise specified including:
- External visual assessment of accessible structure/fabric of each elevation/roof area, each identified building.
- Internal visual inspection of the accessible structure/fabric/roof void each identified building.
- Separate visual assessment/report of, boundary walls, fences and gates within the curtilage.
- Collect data using standardised survey template agreed in advance, using digital technology for this process in order for data to be entered straight into Confirm asset management system.
Capture photographic evidence of defects and key building features with supporting narrative logged in comments and recommendations.
- Assess each building element against grading structure to provide Core Facts summary as agreed in advance.
- Condition Grade A–D
- Priority 1–4 (e.g., Immediate / Year 1 / Years 2–5 / Years 6–10)
- Cost estimates to be provided to support capital planning and investment, maintenance prioritisation, lifecycle investment modelling using market rates and clear assumptions.
- The key deliverables are asset-level reports in electronic format and portfolio-level summaries including PDFs, excel datasets, optional GIS-compatible formats.
- Contractor to provide mobilisation plan and schedule for agreement, access coordination, reporting, and quality assurance processes.
- Reporting format and frequency/review set up-monthly meetings to ensure quality and that programme outputs can be used meaningfully, concerns can be raised and swiftly addressed.
- Access arrangements will be provided listing contact details for premises to be approached to agree access.
If any problems gaining access, details provided of individuals who are able to assist.
As some buildings will be in use during normal working hours all staff of Contractor must carry or wear ID.
- Contractor required to demonstrate compliance with relevant legislation and guidance, with qualified professionals delivering the work.
- Staff of Contractor must have competence aligned to RICS professional standards.
- Survey methodology must follow PFI Asset Condition Playbook principles of standardised inspection and reporting.
- H&S policies and procedures adhered to incl. and not limited to RAMS, urgent defect reporting, adherence to site safety requirements which is mandatory.
---------------
Elements out of scope
- Ground lease assets not required as NLP has no responsibility for building/structures on the land and no statutory obligation or operational requirement to survey these.
- Specialist investigations, intrusive inspections, testing, certification, structural assessments, and specialist mechanical and electrical surveys are excluded from the core commission. Where the condition survey identifies concerns requiring further investigation, the Contractor shall record appropriate recommendations. Any specialist services will only be undertaken where separately instructed by NLP under the Agreement.
- Concealed areas / areas below ground / below ground drainage are excluded.
Soft landscaping excluded.
Consultant not asked to provide a ‘valuation’ of the building/site.
Compliance checks with Disability Discrimination Act and Asbestos Management are excluded Additional information: Economic operators may be excluded from this competition if they are in any of the situations referred to in regulation 58 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015.

Referral-led services are designed for clients who may struggle to access advice through standard routes and require more targeted, intensive support due to multiple and layered issues. The service works collaboratively with local authority services including social workers, support workers, Resilient Families Teams and homelessness prevention services, to plan and deliver support together, ensuring shared outcomes for clients and a seamless and joined up client journey. All advice is delivered by highly skilled advisers, with debt advice provided by FCA-registered staff and subject to robust quality assurance processes. The service holds the Advice Quality Standard (AQS) across Consumer, Debt, Welfare Benefits, Health and Community Care, Disability, Older People, and Students and Young People, as well as the IAQF quality standard, ensuring high-quality specialist advice for those requiring additional and targeted support.

tender.title: Heating, Electrical, Mechanical and Decarbonisation Framework
tender.description: The procurement will establish a single combined, multi-supplier Heating, Electrical, Mechanical and Decarbonisation Framework, not divided into lots, for the provision of works and associated services to domestic and non-domestic properties and buildings, including occupied and void properties. The scope will include, but is not limited to, the provision, supply, installation, replacement, upgrading, servicing, statutory and safety inspection, testing, planned and responsive maintenance and repair of heating, electrical, mechanical, renewable, low-carbon and associated energy systems. Heating works and services will include domestic and commercial/communal systems and equipment using gas, oil, solid fuel, electricity and renewable or low-carbon technologies, including gas and oil boilers, electric storage and panel heaters, electric low-pressure hot water boilers, air source heat pumps, solar-assisted heat pumps, ground source heat pumps, biomass boilers, combined heat and power and micro-CHP systems, heat networks, solar thermal systems, microgeneration installations, wind turbines and other emerging renewable heating and energy technologies. Associated heating and hot-water systems may include hot and cold water services, vented and unvented hot-water cylinders, oil storage tanks, flues, pumps, filling loops, pipework, radiators, low-surface-temperature radiators, fan convectors, controls, smart thermostats and associated electrical controls, together with pipework system cleaning, flushing, de-sludging, de-scaling, sterilisation, water treatment and pipe insulation. The framework will include annual heating safety checks and servicing, Landlord safety and compliance requirements, servicing and maintenance of thermostatic mixing valves and unvented cylinders, planned and responsive repairs, breakdown services, replacement of defective components and systems, void and mutual-exchange checks and emergency and out-of-hours attendance, including 24-hour, 365/366-day services where required. Electrical works and services will include complete and partial rewiring, upgrading, alteration, inspection, testing, certification, Electrical Installation Condition Reports and associated remedial works; consumer units and distribution equipment; RCBOs, RCDs/RCCBs, AFDDs and surge protection devices; main service intake works and associated DNO requirements; earthing and bonding; power, lighting and final circuits; sockets, switches and appliance supplies; immersion heaters; electric showers; connections to heating and boiler systems; external and communal/landlord lighting; supplies to outbuildings and external stores; extract fans and ventilation-related electrical works; doorbells; TV aerial cabling and outlets; photocells, time switches and lighting controls; and associated electrical equipment and systems. The electrical scope will also include domestic fire detection and smoke, heat and carbon-monoxide alarm systems and associated equipment, including interconnection and radio-frequency equipment, together with servicing, maintenance and responsive repair of electric heating installations and 24-hour breakdown provision. Electric vehicle charging infrastructure may be supplied and installed, including associated equipment and services required to provide fully operational charging installations. Mechanical works and services will include mechanical ventilation with heat recovery systems and associated equipment, thermostatic mixing valves, boosted cold-water pump installations and other mechanical equipment associated with heating, hot water, ventilation and energy systems, including servicing and maintenance where required. The decarbonisation and energy scope will include solar photovoltaic systems and associated services, including inverters, controls, metering, monitoring and battery storage systems, together with solar thermal, air source heat pumps, ground source heat pumps, solar-assisted heat pumps, biomass, CHP/micro-CHP, heat networks, wind turbines, mechanical ventilation with heat recovery, smart heating controls, sensors and monitoring equipment and other emerging renewable, low-carbon and energy-efficiency technologies associated with the heating, electrical, mechanical and decarbonisation scope that may be required during the life of the framework. The framework may support retrofit, decarbonisation, ventilation, overheating, indoor-air-quality, EPC improvement, net-zero and future energy-performance requirements, including requirements arising from grant-funded programmes. Retrofit assessment, energy and technical support services may include pre- and post-works Energy Performance Certificates, energy assessments, SAP10 assessments, retrofit assessments, retrofit coordination, retrofit design, PAS 2035 site visits, air-pressure testing, technical monitoring and cavity-wall borescope services, together with associated services. Legionella risk assessments may also be instructed where required in connection with the works and systems covered by the framework. Project management services may be provided for heating, electrical, mechanical, retrofit and decarbonisation programmes, including grant-funded programmes, and may include management and coordination of the appointed supplier's own works and/or coordination of works delivered in collaboration with other framework suppliers. Requirements may be delivered as individual property works, grouped schemes, planned programmes, servicing and compliance programmes, responsive repairs, emergency works, grant-funded projects and larger retrofit or decarbonisation programmes, together with associated services. The framework is intended to remain sufficiently flexible to respond to changes in legislation, technical standards, funding requirements and technology during its term, including the introduction of emerging renewable and energy-efficiency measures falling within the heating, electrical, mechanical and decarbonisation scope. Suppliers appointed to the framework, either directly or through their declared supply chain, will be required to have the capability to deliver the overall range of works and services included within the scope.

tender.procurementMethodRationale:
To meet the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology’s (LMB) multi-omics research objectives across proteomics, lipidomics, and metabolomics, the SCIEX ZenoTOF 8600 system incorporates several crucial, patented technologies:
Patented DJET Ion Guide (US Patent 10475633): Delivers a >10x gain in sensitivity for low-abundance analytes and high mass transmission, allowing efficient transfer of large intact proteins (>100 kDa) to expand proteomics capabilities.
Electron Activated Dissociation (EAD) Cell (US Patent 10014166): Offers tunable fragmentation using variable electron energies (up to 50 eV) and currents, achieving reaction times under 5 ms without compromising data quality—even for singly charged species.
ZenoTRAP Technology (US Patent 7456388): Pairs with EAD to generate exceptionally intense MS/MS spectra for deeper structural elucidation.
No other commercially available system meets the required technical specification to allow MRC LMB to meet their research objectives.

tender.title: Learning Disabilities Short Breaks and Emergency Support
tender.description:
The direct award of a contract for Learning Disability Short Breaks and Emergency Support provision for Adults to Learning Disability Network London for a period of up to 60 months (3 years + 2 year optional extension) from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. This is to provide service continuity whilst building plans are being developed and implemented to re-design the Kingsbridge Road site. Once building works are completed a full competitive tender process will follow. 
The Council’s previous contract with the supplier ended on 31 March 2026.   The supplier has continued to deliver the short breaks services for the Council since that date.  It is intended that the contract will be formerly awarded to the supplier following publication of the Contract Award Notice.   In order to regularise the position, the start date of the contract will be backdated to 1 April 2026 to encompass services provided since the expiry of the previous contract.  This notice is intended to provide visibility of the Council’s intention to formally award the contracts and regulate the arrangements with the supplier by entering into the contracts on or around 14 September 2026 with retrospective effect.  Note that this is an indicative date for signing/entering into the contract and is subject to change.
The contract between Westminster City Council and LDN London is £4,978,600 (excl. VAT) £5,974,320 (inc. VAT) for the full term including extension.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
The Council has statutory duties under the Health and Social Care Act 2008, the Care Act 2014 and other legislation, relating to the health, wellbeing and care of certain individuals.  The Council is required to maintain access to supported and residential accommodation for adults with a learning disability.
Paragraph 5 of Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023 provides a justification for the direct award of public contracts where a particular supplier has exclusive rights which means that only that supplier can supply the goods, services or works required, and there are no reasonable alternatives to those goods, services or work.
RBKC and WCC work together to commission bed-based short breaks from two different premises - Kingsbridge Road and Alision House. The services operate as an integrated bi-borough model, with shared capacity across both premises
The supplier has exclusive property rights to both Kingsbridge Road and Alision House: 
-	The Kingsbridge Road premises were purchased by RBKC in March 2024, the supplier was the existing tenant at the point of acquisition. RBKC is regularising that lease arrangement with the supplier to align with the proposed contracts.  
-	The supplier owns Alison House.
The supplier has confirmed it will not make these premises available to another supplier to deliver the services.
Market engagement and a supplier property survey have been undertaken by the Council which has confirmed that no alternative, suitable premises are currently available.  Accordingly, there is no reasonable alternative to the services being provided by the supplier from the existing premises.
Additionally, the premises at Kingsbridge Road needs significant development work. Capacity at Kingsbridge Road will be significantly reduced during redevelopment works. Having one supplier operating from both premises will provide flexibility enabling the Council to manage capacity and maintain stability and service continuity during the redevelopment period. This further supports that there is no reasonable alternative.
The proposed three-year contract, with an optional two-year extension, will maintain service continuity and enable the Council to meet its statutory duties while the refurbishment works are completed at Kingsbridge Road; as well as providing time for the Council to further explore alternative premises.
Further information can be found in the Council’s decision paper 
https://committees.westminster.gov.uk/documents/s73612/AH26-06%20Direct%20Award%20-%20Short%20Breaks.pdf

tender.title: Provision and Operation of an On-site Private MRI Service
tender.description: Homerton Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust intends to award a contract for the provision and operation of an on-site mobile or relocatable private MRI service at Homerton University Hospital. The service will be exclusively for private patient activity. The Trust intends to award the contract using the Most Suitable Provider process under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023.

lots.description:
Key criteria
1. Value – 35%
The Trust requires a sustainable commercial arrangement which provides an appropriate financial return from use of the Trust estate while placing the ordinary commercial and demand risks associated with the private MRI service with the provider.

The required commercial model comprises: a fixed annual site fee, increasing year on year; and a share of gross private MRI revenue attributable to activity delivered through the service.

The Term length will be for 24 months.

The fixed annual site fee will be payable irrespective of the level of private patient activity achieved. The provider will retain the ordinary commercial and demand risk associated with the private MRI service. The Trust will not guarantee any minimum level of referrals, scans, activity or revenue.

2. Integration, collaboration and service sustainability – 25%
The Trust requires an operating model under which the mobile MRI facility delivers private activity on four days a week. The provider will be responsible for an appropriate power solution, meeting Trust and local authority green initiatives.

3. Quality and innovation – 20%
The Trust requires a safe, high-quality and reliable private MRI service operating from a mobile or relocatable MRI facility on the Trust site. The provider must supply and maintain appropriate MRI equipment, suitably qualified staff, clinical governance and MRI safety arrangements, and a patient environment that is accessible, private and appropriate for private patients.

4. Social value – 12%
The Trust requires the provider to deliver measurable social value through the operation of the service, with particular focus on environmental sustainability, fair employment and benefit to the local community. This should include: minimising the environmental impact of the service, including energy use, emissions and waste; reducing reliance on diesel generation where a technically and commercially feasible lower-carbon alternative is available; supporting fair employment practices and workforce development; and creating appropriate opportunities for local employment or skills development or work experience.

5. Improving access, reducing health inequalities and facilitating choice – 8%
The service should provide an accessible and convenient private MRI pathway for self-pay, insured and other appropriately funded private patients.

Basic selection criteria
Potential providers will also be assessed against the basic selection criteria under the Provider Selection Regime.

Suitability to pursue the activity
Providers must hold all registrations, licences, approvals, insurance and governance arrangements required to provide private MRI diagnostic services from the Trust site.

Economic and financial standing
The provider must demonstrate sufficient economic and financial capacity and resilience to mobilise, operate and sustain the service throughout the proposed contract term and must maintain appropriate levels of professional indemnity and other relevant insurance. Economic and financial standing will be assessed using the Trust's standard Financial and Economic Standing Evaluation methodology. The assessment will include:
- D&B Risk Indicator;
- D&B Failure Score percentile;
- Net cash flow excluding dividend payments, including performance over the most recent three financial years;
- Net surplus/deficit margin before exceptional items, including performance over the most recent three financial years; and
- Gearing ratio, including performance over the most recent three financial years.

Technical and professional ability
The provider must demonstrate the necessary technical and professional ability to deliver MRI services of a comparable nature and scale. This will include appropriate experience, staffing, equipment, MRI safety, maintenance arrangements, clinical and operational capability, and business continuity arrangements. Additional information: This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intended approach notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to this award. The intention is to award a contract using the Most Suitable Provider process.

The award decision makers are:
Daniel Young - Deputy Chief Operating Officer
Alexandra Vekeria - Head of Procurement and Supply Chain

tender.title: UK5 Adults Short Breaks RBKC
tender.description:
The direct award of a contract for Learning Disability Short Breaks and Emergency Support provision for Adults to Learning Disability Network London for a period of up to 60 months (3 years + 2 year optional extension) from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. This is to provide service continuity whilst building plans are being developed and implemented to re-design the Kingsbridge Road site. Once building works are completed a full competitive tender process will follow. 
The Council’s previous contract with the supplier ended on 31 March 2026.   The supplier has continued to deliver the short breaks services for the Council since that date.  It is intended that the contract will be formerly awarded to the supplier following publication of the Contract Award Notice.   In order to regularise the position, the start date of the contract will be backdated to 1 April 2026 to encompass services provided since the expiry of the previous contract.  This notice is intended to provide visibility of the Council’s intention to formally award the contracts and regulate the arrangements with the supplier by entering into the contracts on or around 14 September 2026 with retrospective effect.  Note that this is an indicative date for signing/entering into the contract and is subject to change.
The contract between Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea and LDN London is £2,489,300 (excl. VAT) £2,987,160 (incl. VAT) for the full term including extension.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
The Council has statutory duties under the Health and Social Care Act 2008, the Care Act 2014 and other legislation, relating to the health, wellbeing and care of certain individuals.  The Council is required to maintain access to supported and residential accommodation for adults with a learning disability.
Paragraph 5 of Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023 provides a justification for the direct award of public contracts where a particular supplier has exclusive rights which means that only that supplier can supply the goods, services or works required, and there are no reasonable alternatives to those goods, services or work.
RBKC and WCC work together to commission bed-based short breaks from two different premises - Kingsbridge Road and Alision House. The services operate as an integrated bi-borough model, with shared capacity across both premises
The supplier has exclusive property rights to both Kingsbridge Road and Alision House: 
-	The Kingsbridge Road premises were purchased by RBKC in March 2024, the supplier was the existing tenant at the point of acquisition. RBKC is regularising that lease arrangement with the supplier to align with the proposed contracts.  
-	The supplier owns Alison House.
The supplier has confirmed it will not make these premises available to another supplier to deliver the services.
Market engagement and a supplier property survey have been undertaken by the Council which has confirmed that no alternative, suitable premises are currently available.  Accordingly, there is no reasonable alternative to the services being provided by the supplier from the existing premises.
Additionally, the premises at Kingsbridge Road needs significant development work. Capacity at Kingsbridge Road will be significantly reduced during redevelopment works. Having one supplier operating from both premises will provide flexibility enabling the Council to manage capacity and maintain stability and service continuity during the redevelopment period. This further supports that there is no reasonable alternative.
The proposed three-year contract, with an optional two-year extension, will maintain service continuity and enable the Council to meet its statutory duties while the refurbishment works are completed at Kingsbridge Road; as well as providing time for the Council to further explore alternative premises.
Further information can be found in the Council’s decision paper 
https://rbkc.moderngov.co.uk/committees/documents/s35671/KD1013631R.pdf
