tender.description:
Great Western Railway (GWR) is seeking to establish a multi-supplier framework for the provision of fabrication, structural repair and composite repair services in support of its Train & Rolling Stock (T&RS) maintenance operations.
The objective of this procurement is to establish a reliable, responsive and technically competent supply base capable of supporting GWR with both planned and ad hoc fabrication and repair requirements.
The Framework is divided into the following Lots:
Lot 1 - Metal Fabrication and Non-Structural Repairs: metal fabrication, replacement panel production and non-structural bodywork repairs.
Lot 2 - Structural Repairs: structural repair services to vehicle body shells and load-bearing structures, including specialist welding and associated engineering activities.
Lot 3 - Composite Repairs: specialist repair and refurbishment of composite components and structures.

tender.title: Technical Implementation Partner & Business Change Partner (DASP)
tender.description:
NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is procuring delivery partners for the Donor and Session Programme (DASP), a strategic digital transformation programme to modernise donor engagement, appointment booking, session management and related donor-facing and operational capabilities across blood, platelets and plasma.
The procurement is divided into two Lots:
Lot 1: Technical Implementation Partner
The Technical Implementation Partner will support the technical implementation of the selected CRM Platform and associated digital ecosystem. The scope includes solution design, configuration, integration, data migration, testing, deployment, transition, implementation governance, technical assurance and operational readiness.
Suppliers tendering for Lot 1 must align their Tender Response to one of the eligible CRM Platforms identified in the Invitation to Tender documents. The proposed technical solution, implementation approach and associated commercial submissions must be prepared consistently on the basis of the selected CRM Platform.
Lot 2: Business Change Partner
The Business Change Partner will support the business change, adoption and operational transformation required to implement DASP successfully. The scope includes operating model and workforce transformation, stakeholder engagement, change impact assessment, communications, learning and capability development, adoption planning, business readiness, benefits realisation and transition to business as usual.
NHSBT intends to award a single-supplier contract for each Lot. Suppliers may tender for either Lot or both Lots but must submit a complete and independently compliant Tender Response for each Lot tendered for.
The full requirements, eligible CRM Platforms, procurement procedure, Conditions of Participation, award criteria, evaluation methodology, timetable, contract terms and submission instructions are set out in the Invitation to Tender and associated tender documents available through Atamis under reference C468497.

tender.title: Cleaning of Council  Vehicles and Waste Receptacles
tender.description:
The London Borough of Barnet require a cleaning service to wash the Council’s fleet vehicles and plant, food waste bins within our town centres and ad-hoc washing of containers in different sizes within the borough.
The cleaning service will be divided into 2 LOTS 
LOT 1 Vehicle, Plant and Equipment Washing
LOT 2 Container Washing Services - Regular, scheduled washing of town centre food waste bins and Ad-hoc washing services for all container types and waste streams
Vehicle, Plant and Equipment Washing 
The London Borough of Barnet requires a supplier to deliver comprehensive vehicle washing and cleaning services for its mixed fleet of operational vehicles and plant.
The services include routine, periodic and ad hoc washing for light and heavy vehicles including, refuse collection vehicles, sweepers, winter maintenance gritters, buses and tippers, and preparation of vehicles for MOT and chassis inspections to DVSA standards. Volumes and frequencies are indicative and may vary throughout the contract to reflect operational requirements.
Services will be delivered primarily from the Council’s wash bay facilities at Oakleigh Road Depot. The supplier is responsible for providing all labour, cleaning materials, equipment and PPE, and must comply with all health and safety, environmental, and COSHH regulations. 
Container Washing 
Barnet provides a range of containers of varying types and sizes for the collection of general waste, food waste, recycling, and garden waste. This service requirement covers the washing and cleaning of waste containers used across the borough.
The bin washing service will include:
•Scheduled washing of all town centre food waste bins, and
•An ad-hoc washing service for containers of various sizes, ranging from 200 litre's to 1,100 litre's, and across all waste streams (general waste, recycling, and food waste).
There is a statutory requirement for all Local Authorities in England to implement separate collections of food waste and recycling across all residential property types. To meet this obligation, the council has installed a number of communal food waste bins across the borough, predominantly serving flatted properties within town centres. These bins require cleaning in accordance with an agreed schedule to maintain hygiene standards and operational efficiency.

tender.description:
Broad Horizons Education Trust is currently exploring options for the future provision of its payroll services commencing in September 2027. The Trust currently has an estimated headcount of 1408 employees across 18 sites/academies, processed on a monthly pay cycle.
The purpose of this Request for Information is to engage with potential suppliers prior to any formal procurement to:
Inform our procurement strategy, scope, and specification.
Gauge market interest, capacity, and capabilities.
Understand standard market pricing models, implementation timelines, and risk mitigation strategies.
The primary objectives of this engagement are to:
Gauge current market interest, capacity, and capabilities across service delivery models 
Seek supplier feedback to refine and finalize the procurement strategy, technical specification, and performance KPIs.
Understand commercial and pricing models.
Inform system integration requirements to ensure a successful go-live for September 2027.
Key operational requirements include:
Full and seamless transition
Full management processing of monthly payrolls.
Comprehensive public sector pension scheme administration, returns, and compliance-specifically Teachers' Pensions Scheme (TPS) and Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) 
Pay scales - To be able to cope with Teaching pay scales, support staff pay scale, apprenticeships plus off-scale pay grades where needed
Pay awards and increments To be able to apply pay awards to current staff automatically
For back pay to be automatically calculated
To be able to chose to backdated pay awards to some leavers
To be able to apply increments at different dates for some staff
To be able to apply 'No Increment' for specific contracts
Integration capability with existing HR and Finance systems and simple data input
Integration with MIS - currently Arbor - to provide a 'single source of truth' from which reports and data flows
Access for Employees - To efficiently be able to download payslips, P60s etc.
To efficiently be able to update personal details, including bank account details
Knowledge and experience working with MATs in the education sector.

The Council has awarded a contract for the design, supply, installation and commissioning of ground source heat pump systems to up to 231 dwellings within the Balmoral tower blocks comprising Brecon, Blackdown and Grampian House. The project is funded through the Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund Wave 3 programme, supported by Council match funding, and forms part of the Council's wider housing decarbonisation and fuel poverty reduction objectives.
The contract has been procured via FrameworkX and is subject to the Public Contracts Regulations 2015.

lots.description:
The contract provides for the delivery of energy efficiency improvement works through the replacement of existing electric storage heating and direct electric heating systems with ground source heat pump technology in up to 231 residential properties. The scope includes design, resident liaison, installation, testing, commissioning and associated works required to deliver a compliant and operational system. The contract will support the Council's Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund Wave 3 programme and contribute towards improving energy performance, reducing carbon emissions and lowering household energy costs for residents. The contract term runs until 31 March 2028, in line with funding programme requirements. Additional information: The contract has been awarded by direct award under the Fusion21 framework. The Council was required to mobilise the project within challenging programme timescales associated with the Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund Wave 3 grant. Grant funding is subject to fixed annual expenditure profiles and delays in procurement risked the loss of allocated funding and the Council's ability to deliver the project within the required programme period.
A framework route was selected as the most efficient and economically advantageous procurement mechanism, providing pre-competed terms and demonstrable value for money while enabling accelerated project mobilisation. Market assessment of the relevant framework lot identified a limited number of suitable suppliers capable of delivering the specialist ground source heat pump installation works required for high-rise residential buildings. Of the suppliers available on the framework, one supplier had subsequently entered administration and was therefore unable to undertake the contract, while the remaining alternative supplier was not considered capable of delivering the required services and programme outcomes within the necessary timescales. The appointed contractor was therefore the only available framework supplier able to meet the Council's technical, operational and programme requirements and ensure delivery of the funded scheme within the grant timetable.

deliveryLocation.description: The works will be undertaken within the Balmoral tower blocks, comprising Brecon House, Blackdown House and Grampian House, located within the administrative area of Southend-on-Sea City Council, England.

tender.title: Preliminary Market Engagement: Supply of Printed Materials, Educational Resources and Promotional Products
tender.description:
This preliminary market engagement exercise is being conducted solely for information-gathering purposes only.
Trinity Multi Academy Trust (Trinity) is a growing multi-academy trust serving communities across Yorkshire. The Trust operates a diverse portfolio of primary, secondary, and post-16  academies and is committed to delivering high-quality education, operational excellence, and value for money.
As part of its ongoing commitment to securing high-quality goods and services, Trinity is undertaking a preliminary market engagement exercise to consider if the future development of a potential multi-supplier framework agreement for printed materials, promotional products would be beneficial.
Any  potential framework may include, but is not limited to:
•	School planners and diaries
•	Notebooks
•	Lanyards and identification accessories
•	Brochures and prospectuses
•	Leaflets and flyers
•	Promotional literature
•	Corporate stationery
•	Branded merchandise
•	Marketing and event materials
•	Other associated printed and promotional products
Trinity is considering the potential of a multi-lot framework structure, with multiple suppliers appointed across one or more lots to meet the diverse requirements of its academies and central services.
The lot structure has not yet been determined or considered and will be informed through this market engagement exercise.
The purpose of the engagement is to:
•	Understand the current supplier market and supplier capabilities.
•	Gather feedback on a proposed framework and potential lot structure.
•	Explore innovative products, services, and delivery models.
•	Inform the procurement strategy and framework design.
•	Assist in defining the specification and requirements.
•	Understand sustainability initiatives and added-value offerings available within the market.
This preliminary market engagement exercise is being conducted solely for information-gathering purposes only.
This notice is not a commitment to purchase, a call for competition, or an invitation to tender. Participation in this engagement exercise will not guarantee any future business opportunity. Information provided by suppliers will be used only to inform the Trust's procurement strategy, framework design, specification, and requirements.
Should Trinity decide to proceed with a formal procurement process, the opportunity will be advertised through the appropriate public procurement channels to ensure all interested suppliers are notified and have the opportunity to participate.

tender.title: London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme
tender.description:
London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme
Indicative Contract Value: Up to £2900,000 excl. VAT 
Contract Duration: 1 March 2027 – 31 March 2029 with option to extend to 31 March 2030.
This market warming session will be delivered jointly with the VRU's Tertiary Service. The two programmes form complementary elements of the VRU's tertiary violence reduction offer for young people affected by violence and exploitation. While the Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme will provide specialist youth workers embedded across Mayoral youth club settings to identify risk, build trusted relationships and connect young people to support, the redesigned tertiary service will provide intensive, specialist and longer-term support for young people experiencing established, escalating, or entrenched violence and exploitation. Together, these programmes aim to strengthen London's pathway of support for vulnerable young people through earlier identification, stronger partnership working and improved access to specialist interventions.
The London Violence Reduction Unit. The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London. 
The VRU invests in interventions at critical moments to keep young people safe in and out of school and at the key touchpoints that influence a young person’s journey; early years and families, education, positive opportunities, youth work, and communities and place. The Mayor of London has increased investment in London’s Youth Clubs. Across 32 London boroughs and the City of London, a £30 million programme is funding youth clubs to extend and expand their existing offer into weekday evenings, weekends, and school holidays – when young people need safe spaces the most – and provide specialist support to those facing the greatest challenges. 
This investment strengthens youth clubs as trusted community spaces – where connections are made, young people feel safe and valued, and opportunities are created, all with support from trusted adults. The programme will help community organisations reach more young people aged 14–24 years old and strengthen the quality and sustainability of their provision. It will do this by delivering an increased universal, open-access provision, and targeted specialised support for young people facing greater challenges. 
For more information on this specific Youth Clubs programme, please see The Mayor's investment in youth clubs | London City Hall.  
Safety is a core outcome of this Mayoral investment in youth clubs. Whilst it will provide universal youth provision alongside targeted support, some young people will require specialist interventions beyond the expertise and capacity of local delivery partners.  
It has been agreed that a London-wide Safety Offer sits alongside the core Youth Clubs programme.   
Drawing on its regional oversight and networks across London, alongside seven years of experience and expertise in commissioning impactful violence reduction programmes, the VRU is looking to commission a specialist organisation to provide additional capacity to connect with the Mayoral funded youth clubs across the 32 boroughs.   
This provider will deliver a pan-London service providing specialised youth workers, who will be embedded across the 33 Mayoral Youth Clubs, who will provide targeted support for young people experiencing or at risk of violence and exploitation, offer support to enhance feelings of safety and boost connections and pathways into wider specialist services.  
Description of the Service
The future service will operate as a pan-London tertiary intervention with strengthened local delivery through dedicated, specialised youth workers for each Mayoral Youth Club area, with a minimum of 2:1 borough to youth worker ratio.   
The aim of the Safety Programme will be to provide a visible, connected and meaningful presence across the 33 Mayoral Youth Clubs to support children and young people who are affected by, or vulnerable to, violence and exploitation. Its purpose is to identify those at risk (working with the youth club provider), provide direct support, make referrals into appropriate services and interventions and enhance feelings of safety. 
The VRU will commission a specialist organisation to deliver the Safety Programme. This additional resource will establish a network of specialist practitioners who will work alongside funded Youth Club partnerships, providing additional capacity and expertise to identify, engage, and support young people who face higher levels of risk. They will work with local partnerships to build trusted relationships with young people, provide targeted interventions and support, and help young people access wider opportunities and services.  
The Safety Programme will operate as a pan-London network, enabling practitioners to share learning, insight and effective practice across boroughs and communities. This will help strengthen local responses to emerging issues, support partnership working and contribute to the wider learning and development of the programme.    
The service will contribute to the Violence Reduction Unit's public health approach to preventing and reducing violence in London, by preventing harm, identifying and addressing risk factors, and improving outcomes for children and young people.
The service is expected to: 
•Provide specialised youth workers who build trusted relationships with children and young people who may be at risk of harm, supporting them to access the Mayoral youth club as a safe space.
•Provide a regular presence within the Mayoral youth clubs, working with youth club staff to identify young people with existing or potential risk and need for further support.
•Assess needs and vulnerabilities of children and young people identified as at risk, including those impacted by exploitation, extra familial harm, online and digital harms and domestic abuse.  
•Provide targeted support and engagement, including 1-1 support for children and young people at greater risk of harm, holding casework where appropriate.  Prioritise tertiary young people, with support extending to secondary young people as capacity allows.
•Facilitate access to appropriate statutory, community and specialist support services through referrals and where needed building connections and support pathways, including connecting with families /parents /guardians as appropriate to ensure a whole family approach.
•Undertake contextual safeguarding assessments, working with the youth club providers and local authority partners, to assess contextual risk of youth club and surrounding environments, and deliver peer group contextual interventions where appropriate. 
•Deliver workshops and group work aimed at increasing safety of young people attending the youth club and support awareness of risk, based on identified local concerns/need. 
•Work collaboratively with mayoral youth clubs and wider statutory agencies to strengthen the connections and pathways between the many safety programmes held both by VCS and public authorities; and do so through a place-based approach.   
•Strengthen local partnership responses to emerging safeguarding and violence-related issues through sharing understanding of emerging risks, contextual safeguarding and issues impacting children and young people in local areas.   
•Operate as a pan-London network, share intelligence and effective practice across London through a connected practitioner network. 
•Contribute to reductions in vulnerability and harm and improving outcomes for children and young people.  
•Embed trauma-informed practice, lived experience and cultural sensitivity throughout service delivery. 
Target Audience
Young people aged 14 to 24 living in London who are identified as experiencing, or are at significant risk of violence, criminal exploitation, sexual exploitation and related harms. Scope of Delivery
The provider will be expected to deliver a consistent pan-London service of support for children and young people at risk across the 33 mayoral youth club partnerships, through strong local relationships with Mayoral Youth Club Providers, Local Authorities, safeguarding partners, community organisations and specialist services.
Core elements are expected to include specialist youth engagement and support, identifying and assessing needs, facilitating targeted referrals and engagement with wider services, contextual safeguarding and where appropriate, casework.

Specialist Youth Work and Engagement 
The Safety Programme seeks to enhance the capacity of Youth Club partnerships to prevent violence and exploitation, improve safeguarding and ensure young people receive timely, appropriate support.

•Needs assessments and referrals to appropriate services.
•Casework and coordination with statutory and specialist services.
•Contextual safeguarding assessments and interventions.

Please note, the Authority is not requesting any feedback as part of this round of Engagement. 
1. To express an interest, participants must first be registered on the Home Office's eSourcing Portal (JAGGAER). If you have not yet registered, this can be done online at  https://homeoffice.app.jaggaer.com/web/login.html by following the Register Here Link.  
2. Please note that, to register, you must have a valid D-U-N-S number (as provided by Dun & Bradstreet) for the organisation which you are registering, who will be entering into a contract if invited to do so.  
3. Registering on JAGGAER will not provide immediate access to this Preliminary Market Engagement. Once you have registered on JAGGAER, a registered user can express an interest for a specific procurement.  
This is done by emailing LITUK-2-ProjectTeam@homeoffice.gov.uk with the following:  
- Email subject line: LITUK Procurement - Expression of Interest 
- Email to include: Organisation name (as registered on JAGGAER), D-U-N-S number, Contact name, E-mail address and Telephone number. 
4. Once the above steps are completed, participants will be granted access to the Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) event in JAGGAER. 
5. Participants should then complete and return their signed NDA, via JAGGAER, in order to be added to the Preliminary Market Engagement event once live, on 11 September 2026. 
6. Participants should ensure that they leave enough time to submit the signed NDA and written response in time for the Preliminary Market Engagement close date of 09 October 2026 at 17:00 (BST).  
Please note: if you have previously signed a Home Office NDA for other Projects, you are still required to sign a new NDA and follow the process above. Once you have completed the process above, you will be added to the Engagement Event.

tender.title: Preliminary Market Engagement Round 3 for the Life in the UK (LITUK) Secure Digital Test and Digital Online Learning Materials Service
tender.description:
The Home Office (HO) is the government department responsible for safeguarding the nation through border control, immigration, passport issuance, policing, fire services, counter-terrorism and drugs policies. 
UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) plays an integral role in delivering this vision, managing millions of applications annually, enabling foreign nationals to visit, study, work or settle in the UK. As part of the evolution of existing services, UKVI pursues the transformation and modernisation of services in a manner that enhances customer experience and ensures accurate and efficient outcomes. One of the core services delivered by UKVI is the Life in the UK test, an essential component of the route to settlement in the UK and to UK citizenship. 
The Life in the UK Secure Digital Test and Digital Online Learning Materials Service (LITUK) Project is procuring a new service; enabling the continued delivery of front-end services, balancing continuity with improvements and transformation. 
LITUK aims to move to a 'Digital-by-Default' approach, while upholding the rigorous standards necessary to support UKVI immigration decisions. The successful provider will deliver a service that combines technological innovation with security assurance, enabling customers to demonstrate their knowledge of life in the UK with confidence and convenience throughout their UK immigration journey. 
The purpose of this second round of Preliminary Market Engagement is to gather insights from the market regarding the desired solution, which will inform and support Departmental decision-making processes. At this stage, no final decisions have been made regarding the preferred solution.
Please Note: the content of this Preliminary Market Engagement Notice may be subject to change.

tender.title: London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) Tertiary Service , formally known as Violence & Exploitation Support Service (VESS)
tender.description:
London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) Tertiary Service , formally known as Violence & Exploitation Support Service (VESS)
Indicative Contract Value: Up to £11,493,534 excl. VAT 
Contract Duration: 1 June 2027 – 31 May 2029 with option to extend to 31 May 2030
This market warming session will be delivered jointly with the VRU's forthcoming Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme. The two programmes form complementary elements of the VRU's tertiary violence reduction offer for young people affected by violence and exploitation. While the Mayoral Youth Clubs Safety Programme will provide specialist youth workers embedded across Mayoral youth club settings to identify risk, build trusted relationships and connect young people to support, the redesigned tertiary service will provide intensive, specialist and longer-term support for young people experiencing established, escalating, or entrenched violence and exploitation. 
Together, these programmes aim to strengthen London's pathway of support for vulnerable young people through earlier identification, stronger partnership working and improved access to specialist interventions.
The London Violence Reduction Unit
The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London. 
The VRU invests in interventions at critical moments to keep young people safe in and out of school and at the key touchpoints that influence a young person’s journey; early years and families, education, positive opportunities, youth work, and communities and place.
Project Background
The Violence and Exploitation Support Service (VESS), also known as The Safe Place, was launched in June 2024 to provide coordinated, holistic support for children, young people and families affected by violence and exploitation in London. The service provides specialist support for young people aged 11 to 25 affected by violence and exploitation through an alliance of organisations delivering housing support, advocacy, mentoring, mental health support and other specialist interventions. The current contract expires in June 2027. 
Young people aged 11 to 25 living in London who are experiencing, or are at significant risk of, entrenched violence, criminal exploitation, sexual exploitation and related harms. Particular consideration will be given to young adults, young people with complex safeguarding needs, and those facing barriers to engagement with mainstream services.
Following stakeholder engagement, needs analysis and review of learning from current delivery, the VRU intends to procure a redesigned tertiary service focused on young people experiencing established, escalating or entrenched violence and exploitation. The future model reflects evidence highlighting the importance of trusted relationships, trauma informed practice, specialist support, and strong local partnerships.
Key themes emerging from this work include:
•The need for a clearer focus on young people experiencing entrenched violence and exploitation.
•Greater emphasis on trusted adult relationships and long-term support.
•Stronger transitional safeguarding support for young adults aged 18 to 25.
•Improved local partnership and borough-level integration.
•Enhanced specialist provisions around housing, mental health, education, employment and family support.
•Improved referral pathways and engagement approaches for young people who are least likely to access traditional services.
•Greater recognition of sexual exploitation alongside criminal exploitation.
•Increased focus on neurodiversity, inclusion, and cultural competence. 
The redesigned service is expected to become the VRU's flagship tertiary intervention for young people at risk, and those experiencing the highest levels of vulnerability to violence and exploitation
Description of the Service
The future service will operate as a pan-London tertiary intervention with strengthened local delivery through cluster-based arrangements. It is expected to provide intensive, flexible and relationship-based support; specialist expertise in housing, mental health, education, employment and training; support for young adults aged 18 to 25; specialist responses for girls and young women; and improved pathways for criminal and sexual exploitation. A team-around-the-worker approach will support case workers with specialist advocates and navigators.
The service is expected to:
•Provide dedicated lead practitioners who build trusted relationships with young people.
•Deliver flexible, community-based support in locations that are accessible and comfortable for young people.
•Operate through a partnership model that combines core casework with specialist expertise.
•Strengthen local partnerships and referral pathways while maintaining a pan-London offer.
•Support young people through a long-term journey of engagement, stabilisation, change, and sustained outcomes.
•Embed trauma-informed practice, lived experience and cultural competence throughout service delivery. 
Target Audience
Young people aged 11 to 25 living in London who are experiencing, or are at significant risk of, or currently entrenched in violence, criminal exploitation, sexual exploitation. 
Scope of Delivery
The provider partnership will be expected to deliver a consistent pan-London service whilst maintaining strong local relationships with boroughs, safeguarding partners, community organisations and specialist services. Core elements are expected to include targeted referrals, intensive casework, housing support, family support, education and employment pathways, mental health navigation, support for neurodiverse young people, transitional safeguarding and county lines rescue capability.
Indicative Service Model
While the final specification has not yet been developed, current thinking suggests the service may include:
Core Specialist Casework
Dedicated Violence and Exploitation Practitioners providing intensive support and care for coordination for young people. 
Specialist Pathways and Expertise
Potential specialist functions may include:
•Housing and accommodation support.
•Mental health and therapeutic support.
•Education, Employment and Training (EET).
•SEND and neurodiversity expertise.
•Family support.
•Support for girls and young women.
•Transitional safeguarding for young adults aged 18-25. 
County Lines Rescue Function
The recommissioned service is expected to retain a county lines rescue and relocation capability, although the final model is currently under consideration.
Timeframe: The contract is expected to commence on 1 June 2027 following a mobilisation period from March to May 2027. The initial term will be two years with an option to extend for one additional year.

procurementMethodRationaleLegalBasis.description: Direct Award Justification - Schedule 5, Paragraph 41(1), Procurement Act 2023

documents.description: Not published

tender.riskDetails:
Single Source Justification for 6X VIDS-210/LS CABLES
Background
TAIPAN has replaced the Mobile Artillery Monitoring Battlefield Radar (MAMBA) fleet, introducing a new Weapon Locating Radar (WLR) capability into service. As part of this capability, a new BOWMAN communications system has been installed on each platform.
In accordance with JSP 604, Part 2, Volume 2, 4850-TacCIS, all new BOWMAN installations are required to undergo a Connectivity Assurance Test (CAT) prior to being accepted into service.
Situation
During the pre-CAT Installation Certification Assessment for the TacCIS installation in Taipan (MAMBA) platforms, an observation was raised identifying that the VIDS-210/LS cable connecting the GPS Applique to the HCDR was not connected. The User advised the cable connector does not fit on the HCDR.
Further investigation determined that the connector is missing the locating lugs required for attachment to the HCDR. This appears to be a manufacturing defect affecting all five TAIPAN platforms. As a result, the GPS Applique cannot be connected to the HCDR, potentially preventing the HCDR from forming part of the BOWMAN network and jeopardising successful completion of the mandatory CAT process.
TAS assess each observation made against each TacCIS installation requirement and considered what affect, if any, they have on the safety, security, supportability and performance of the TacCIS system. This has resulted in the above observation being categorised as:
Essential - the design would have a substantial impact on the safety, security, supportability and performance of the TacCIS installation.
To rectify the defect and enable the platforms to achieve connectivity assurance certification, replacement VIDS-210/LS cables are required.
Regulation
Direct Award Justification - Schedule 5, Paragraph 41(1), Procurement Act 2023
The Authority proposes to directly award a contract to General Dynamics United Kingdom Limited (GDUK) for the supply of six (6) VIDS-210/LS cables (GDUK Part Number GD400410-0380-05).
A direct award is justified as only GDUK, as the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Design Authority for the BOWMAN system and associated components, can provide the exact cable assembly required to restore the affected installations and ensure compliance with the certified BOWMAN configuration. No reasonable alternative supplier has been identified that can provide an equivalent, assured and fully compatible cable assembly suitable for use within the BOWMAN architecture.
The replacement cables are required no later than 26 February 2027 to support CAT activities and prevent delays to the entry into service of the TAIPAN capability. Accordingly, the Authority is satisfied that the criteria for direct award under Schedule 5, Paragraph 41(1) of the Procurement Act 2023 are met.

criteria.description:
SPD Question 4A.1 Trade Registers
It is a requirement of this tender that if the Tenderer is UK based they must hold a valid registration with Companies House. Where the
Tenderer is UK based but not registered at Companies House they must be able to verify to the SPA’s satisfaction that they are trading
from the address provided in the tender and under the company name given.
Tenderers within the UK must confirm if they are registered under Companies House within this question.
If the Tenderer is based out-with the UK they must be enrolled in the relevant professional or trade register appropriate to their country as
described in Schedule 5 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015.
SPD Question 4A.2 Authorisation/Membership
Bidders should refer to the published Contract Notice Document and ITT which can be found within Public Contract Scotland Tender
which details the required authorisation or memberships required for each Lot. Due to the character limit this cannot be added to the
published Contract Notice on Public Contract Scotland.

SPD Question 4B5 Insurances
It is a requirement of this Framework that Tenderers hold, or can commit to obtain prior to the commence of any subsequently awarded
Framework, indicated below:
The Tenderer should include with its tender insurance certificates confirming that the Tenderer maintains insurance policies which meet or
exceed the below requirements. The selected Supplier must maintain these levels of insurance throughout the period of the framework
(subject in the case of professional indemnity insurance to such insurance remaining available at commercially reasonable rates and upon
commercially reasonable terms).
(a) Professional Indemnity insurance: FIVE MILLION POUNDS (5,000,000 GBP) in respect of each occurrence and in the annual
aggregate, with a minimum of 2 automatic reinstatements of the full annual limit of Five Million Pounds (5,000,000 GBP);
Professional Indemnity insurance (Lot 8 and 9 only): TWO MILLION POUNDS (2,000,000 GBP) in respect of each occurrence and in the annual aggregate, with a minimum of 2 automatic reinstatements of the full annual limit of Two Million Pounds (2,000,000 GBP);
(b) Employer’s Liability insurance: FIVE MILLION POUNDS (5,000,000 GBP) for any one occurrence or series of occurrences arising out of any one event; and
(c) Public Liability insurance: TEN MILLION POUNDS (10,000,000 GBP) for any one occurrence or series of occurrences arising out of any one event.
SPD Question 4B6 Financial Standing:
The Authority will access a Credit safe report for a Tenderers organisation and use the information contained within to assist with the
assessment of the Tenderer’s economic and financial standing. Tenders are asked to provide their company number within the ESPD to
allow the Authority to access a Credit Safe Report.
Within such reports, the risk of business failure is expressed as a score of 30 or below (high risk of business failure). In the event that a
company is determined to have a risk failure rating of 30 and below i.e. that the company is considered to have a high risk of business
failure, the submission will not be considered further.
If you are successful in the award of this contract and your risk failure rating falls below 30 then the SPA reserve the right to remove you
from this contract. It is the Contractor’s responsibility to ensure that the information held by Credit Safe is accurate and up to date.
For the avoidance of doubt, the SPA will request a report from Credit Safe following the closing date for the receipt of the Tenders to
ensure that the most up to date information is used. Where you are not registered on credit safe e.g. charitable organisations or new start
companies/ Sole Traders with less than 3 years trading history, discretionary powers are available to the Director of Finance to consider
abbreviated accounts along with bankers references etc.
Tenderers should be aware that any outstanding County Court Judgements will have a detrimental effect on the rating held by Credit Safe
and it is your responsibility to ensure that the information held by Credit Safe is accurate and up to date- failure to do so will result in
rejection of your submission.
IMPORTANT NOTE: This requirement is not applicable to Sole Traders/ Charities. Sole Traders/ Charities may be required to provide a
bankers reference if successful.

SPD Question 4C.1.2 Technical and Professional Ability
With reference to the nature and details of the services that are the subject matter of this tender, relevant examples are to be provided of the services undertaken by the Tenderer in the last 3 years and must be similar value to the contract being procured.
FOR EACH LOT-Tenderer`s will be required to provide evidence of having the necessary capacity and capability to deliver the requirements for the lots they are bidding for.
Two (2) examples of the provision of similar services for each individual Lot (should bidders bid for more than 1 lot) will be requested and must be from within the last 3 years for goods and services.
If Tenderers are unable to provide two (2) examples the tenderer may be required to explain why examples cannot be provided.
If available, copies of completion certificates or customers' written declaration which validates the examples you have provided.
Guidance
If you cannot provide certificates or customer declarations the Authority may choose to contact customers cited directly in order to validate
the experience examples you have provided without any further reference to you.

tender.title: Provision, Installation and Operation of Christmas Attractions in Albert Square Manchester
tender.description:
Manchester's annual festive programme is one of the most celebrated in Europe, attracting millions of visitors and creating a vibrant seasonal atmosphere across the city. As part of Manchester City Council's commitment to enhancing the city's cultural and event offering, we seek competent proposals for the delivery of Albert Square's Christmas attraction from 2027 onwards.
Historically, Manchester's Christmas activities have included the award-winning Christmas Markets, an ice rink at Cathedral Gardens, and a range of family-friendly installations. With the full reopening of Albert Square following Town Hall regeneration works, the Council aims to create a world-class festive destination that complements the existing city-wide offer and strengthens Manchester's reputation as a leading winter destination.
The requirement is for a Christmas attraction in Albert Square, operating seven days a week during the festive period (November to early January), featuring the following core elements:
An ice rink, managed and installed by the appointed operator, providing a safe and authentic skating experience for visitors. The proposal should include rink size, capacity, and associated facilities such as skate hire and changing areas.
A varied food and beverage offering, aligned with the Manchester Christmas Markets ethos, catering for diverse tastes and dietary requirements while delivering a sense of place.
Family-friendly festive attractions, which may include (but are not limited to) an ice bar, curling rink, ice sculptures, an observatory wheel, rides, funfair, or other creative installations that enhance the visitor experience and differentiate Albert Square from other UK festive destinations.
Seasonal theming and dressing, including Christmas decorations, lighting features, projections, music, and branded signage to create a cohesive and welcoming environment.
The successful operator will be responsible for full site management, including stewarding, first aid, staffing, security, emergency procedures, and compliance with all licensing and health and safety requirements. Marketing and promotion of the attraction will also form part of the operator's obligations, working in partnership with Manchester City Council to maximise visitor engagement.
It is anticipated that to deliver these elements, the winning contractor will need to source equipment and collaborate with specialist providers where necessary. All proposals should demonstrate creativity, operational competence, and a commitment to sustainability, social value, and community engagement.

SPD will be scored on a pass/fail basis.
Question scoring methodology for Award Criteria outlined in Invitation to Tender.
0 - Unacceptable. Nil or inadequate response. Fails to demonstrate an ability to meet the requirement.
1 - Poor. Response is partially relevant but generally poor. The response addresses some elements of the requirement but contains insufficient/limited detail or explanation to demonstrate how the requirement will be fulfilled.
2 - Acceptable. Response is relevant and acceptable. The response addresses a broad understanding of the requirement but may lack details on how the requirement will be fulfilled in certain areas.
3 - Good. Response is relevant and good. The response is sufficiently detailed to demonstrate a good understanding and provides details on how the requirements will be fulfilled.
4 - Excellent. Response is completely relevant and excellent overall. The response is comprehensive, unambiguous and demonstrates a thorough understanding of the requirement and provides details of how the requirement will be met in full.

tender.title: 704_26 Outsourced Catering Services and Procurement Support
tender.description:
ESPO is a public sector-owned professional buying organisation offering a comprehensive range of procurement services, including access to over 100 free-to-access framework solutions for the wider public sector.
This procurement establishes a framework to assist customers in education, social care and all other public sectors with outsourcing their catering services, including providing access to procurement consultants who can assist customers with this (in outsourcing their catering services).
The Framework is divided into 4 lots.
For any additional details please also refer to https://www.espo.org/outsourced-catering-services-and-procurement-support-704-26.html (or otherwise see https://www.espo.org/procurement-frameworks).

participationFees.description:
As a public body, ESPO have a statutory obligation to recover the costs incurred in the management of this Framework. This obligation is met by means of a Framework Fee which will be payable by the Suppliers to ESPO based on the total turnover of business conducted by them under the Framework.
A 0.5% Fee applies for Lots 1-3, and a 4% Fee with maximum cap per customer contract of £250 applies to Lot 4 only.

frameworkAgreement.buyerCategories: As a Centralised procurement authority as defined in the Procurement Act 2023, the Framework is open for use by Public Bodies (defined at https://www.espo.org/amfile/file/download/file/9608/) that also fall into one of the following classifications of user throughout all administrative regions of the UK: Local Authorities; Educational Establishments (including Academies); Central Government Departments and Agencies; Police, Fire & Rescue and Coastguard Emergency Services; NHS and HSC Bodies, including Ambulance Services; Registered Charities; Registered Social Landlords; The Corporate Office of the House of Lords, The Corporate Officer of the House of Commons; or any public body established by or under the Scotland Act 1998 or any Act of the Scottish Parliament. Details on general classification of end user establishments and geographical areas are available at: https://www.espo.org/legal
frameworkAgreement.description:
Customers wishing to buy Services via the Framework will do so in the following way(s) in accordance with section 45 of the Procurement Act 2023 (and any subsequent amendment or re-enactment thereof):
Call-off without competition (LOT 4 ONLY)
Only customers accessing Lot 4 will be able to access the Framework by ‘calling-off’ Services from a Supplier identified who is a) included in the Framework, b) suitable for meeting the Customer’s specific needs, c) within the geographical region/sub-region of the Customer, and d) identified as offering the most advantageous solution to the Customer’s requirements, based on the Framework pricing and the additional benefits offered by each Supplier.
Call-off with competition (Further Competitive Selection Process)
Customers accessing all lots will be able to 'call-off' by conducting a further competitive selection process amongst those Suppliers identified in the Framework as being able to supply the required Services. This means that not all competitive selection processes will necessarily include all the Suppliers - a customer will only invite those Suppliers that are included in the Framework for the particular type and location of contract required. Customers will assess the suppliers as set out in the terms and conditions of the Framework.
Please note that once this Framework is established, the right is reserved by the Customer when running a further competitive selection process, to invite the Suppliers to participate in an eAuction.

tender.title: Technology Enabled Community Care (TECC)
tender.description:
The contracting authority intends to establish a framework agreement for Technology Enabled Community Care, aimed at facilitating the provision of products and services that enhance independence, safety, accessibility, and communication for individuals with diverse needs. 
The framework will encompass the following areas: 
• Communication Aids, Interface Devices, Environmental Controls and Maintenance: Including Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) products, environmental control systems, access devices, accessories, environmental controllers, and associated maintenance and support services. 
• Mounting Devices: Equipment and solutions designed to securely mount assistive technology and communication devices to wheelchairs, furniture, beds, and other fixtures. 
• Patient Alarms and Sensors: Products and systems that support monitoring, alerting, and safety, including patient alarms, sensors, and related assistive technologies. 
• Lone Worker Devices: Devices and systems designed to monitor, support, and enhance the safety of individuals working alone. 
Note: For future tenders the following requirements will apply: 
• ISO Certification: Tenderers must have ISO 9001: 2015 or BS EN ISO 13485:2016 or Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDAP) accredited by the United Kingdom Accreditation Service (or international equivalent) to cover all segments of the Tenderer's and the product's supply chain. This should include, but not be limited to, sales, manufacturing, storage and distribution ('ISO Certification'). Link for acceptable alternatives https://iaf.nu/en/accreditation-bodies/ ('Notified Bodies') 
• CE Certification and Declaration of Conformity certificates are required where applicable to be presented at submission stage of the tender. 
• Modern Slavery for Tenderers that have an annual turnover of at least £36 million must have a link to their modern slavery statement on their website 
• Modern Slavery Assessment Tool (MSAT) Tenderers must have a score of 41% or above within 12months of the Tender Publication Date via https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/ 
• Evergreen Sustainable Supplier Assessment - Tenderers will need to have completed the assessment and achieved Level 1 within 12months of the Tender Publication Date. Link for instructions and access for this assessment: https://www.england.nhs.uk/nhs-commercial/central-commercial-function-ccf/evergreen/ 
• Carbon Reduction Plan (CRP): Tenders must have a valid CRP link on their website that meets the requirements of PPN 006 as outlined in the PPN, OR Where Supplier has no website, the CRP is provided in PDF format that meets the requirements of PPN 006 as outlined in the PPN, OR Excused in exceptional circumstances 
• Cyber Security: If you handle patient or personal data, or provide any IT systems, services, or devices you will need to have a Cyber Security Essentials Plus Certificate

Provider Selection Regime (Wales) 2025 – Notice of Intention to Award
As required by the Health Services (Provider Selection Regime) (Wales) Regulations 2025, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board gives notice of its intention to award a contract under the Most Suitable Provider Process for the provision of NHS General Dental Services within North Denbighshire.
North Wales has a resident population of 686,909 persons (Census 2021) living across approximately 2,500 square miles and includes a mixture of coastal, rural and urban communities. Access to NHS dental services remains a significant challenge across the region, with over 21,000 patients currently awaiting access through the Dental Access Portal. North Denbighshire was identified as a priority area for additional NHS dental capacity and access improvements.
To support this requirement, the Health Board undertook an Expression of Interest (EOI) process to understand current provider capacity, capability and interest in delivering NHS General Dental Services within the locality. Following completion of the EOI process, shortlisted providers were invited to participate in a structured Most Suitable Provider (MSP) assessment.
For the avoidance of doubt, this award is being undertaken under the Health Services (Provider Selection Regime) (Wales) Regulations 2025. The Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and the Procurement Act 2023 do not apply to this award.
The decision-makers comprise representatives from; Assistant Director of Primary Care, Primary Care Contracting Team, Clinical Governance, Finance, Primary Care Dental Practice Advisors.
The proposed award recommendation is subject to completion of the Health Board's governance processes and Board approval.
Publication date: 11 September 2026
Deadline for representations: 25 September 2026
Any representations or queries regarding the proposed award must be submitted by email to: BCU.DentalContractingTeam@wales.nhs.uk
Representations received after 25 September 2026 will not be considered.
(WA Ref:170045)

tender.title: Drummond Community Centre Refurbishment
tender.description:
Drummond Community Centre is an important community facility serving residents across Grange Park and the wider Hedge End area. The proposed improvement works will enhance the building both internally and externally, ensuring it remains a welcoming, functional and well-maintained facility for the community for years to come.
The Drummond Community Centre was built in 1990; it is single storey with a brick base and aluminium pitched roof. The roof sky lights were replaced in 2022. It has a full height roof with beams. The main hall lights were replaced with LED in 2023.
We are seeking a principal contractor to carry out a sympathetic refurbishment to fit with the surrounding area and usage of the building.

tender.title: Group Plant & Tool Hire Tender
tender.description:
MAG is seeking to award a contract for the provision of Plant and Tool Hire services across its UK airports through a Competitive Flexible Procedure in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023.
The successful supplier will be required to provide access to a comprehensive range of plant, powered access equipment, lifting equipment, accommodation units, generators, pumps, survey equipment, temporary site equipment, tools and associated accessories to support operational, maintenance and construction activities across Manchester, Stansted and East Midlands Airport. The contract will also support the requirements of approved third-party contractors operating on MAG sites.
The appointed supplier will be responsible for the supply, delivery, collection and ongoing support of hire assets, together with management information and spend reporting to support effective contract management and continuous improvement throughout the contract term.
The procurement seeks to establish a single contractual arrangement with a supplier capable of delivering a responsive, compliant and commercially competitive service across all MAG locations.
Bidders will be evaluated against the following criteria:
Technical
Commercial
ESG
Legal and Contractual Compliance

releases.description:
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention to award notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contract Regulations 2015/Procurement Act 2023 do not apply to this award. The standstill period begins on the day after the publication of this notice. Representations by providers must be made to decision makers, in writing to Lisa.Buckley@uhnm.nhs.uk by 23rd September 2026.

This contract has not yet formally been awarded; this notice serves as an intention to award under the PSR.

Decision Makers:
The Director of Procurement and the Trust's Chief Financial Officer (Delegated to Director of Operational Finance) approved the decision to award via Option C on 25/08/2026.

No Conflicts of Interest have been declared by the Individuals making the decision.

The basis for awarding awarding this proposed Contract was in accordance with the PSR Regulations and included (a) The Authority satisfying itself that the considerable change threshold was not met and (b) The Authority satisfying itself that the existing provider is satisfying its existing contract and will likely satisfy the proposed contract to a sufficient standard.

The decision was supported based on performance assessed against the PSR Key Criteria:

Key Criteria 1: Quality and Innovation (Weighting 45%)
Key Criteria 2: Value (Weighting 25%)
Key Criteria 3: Integration, Collaboration and Service Sustainability (10%)
Key Criteria 4: Improving Access, Reducing Health Inequalities and Facilitating Choice (Weighting 10)
Key Criteria 5: Social Value (Weighting 10%)

The assessment determined that the existing provider is satisfying it's performance against the current contract and were likely to continue to meet the key criteria under the new contract.

tender.title: Gallery 33 - Principal Contractor
tender.description:
In September 2027, we will open a new, permanent gallery at South Kensington dedicated to building a positive connection to nature in our very youngest audiences - aged 4-7 years old - and their adults.    This brand-new gallery will be a place where visitors delight in the dazzling variety of life on Earth, from the very small to the very tall, and discover that all life – including us! – share the same needs. We all need to breathe, eat, move, communicate and grow to survive and often depend on each other to do this. Together, we are all part of this great, big, weird and wonderful natural world. It will deliver inspiring stories that celebrate diversity and welcome in the widest possible audience of children and their adults. It will combine our world-leading collections, with hands-on and multi-sensory interactives that evoke joy, empathy and care.   This project supports our Strategy and Mission to 2031 and our vision of a future where both people and the planet thrive, with a mission to create advocates for the planet. By appealing to visitors’ sense of kindness, their curiosity, and their imagination, this gallery will lay the foundations of advocacy for nature at a young age, foster a lifelong appreciation of the natural world and build a positive connection to nature in early childhood. 
Gallery 33 (working title) will replace the current Creepy Crawlies gallery on the ground floor the Grade 1 listed Waterhouse East Building and refurbishing the space for the new exhibition. It will open in September 2027 as a free, permanent gallery, and is expected to welcome millions of visitors over a 25-year lifespan. This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to create a new gallery which positions children at the heart of our Museum and inspire the next generation of children to start their lifelong journey of advocacy for the planet.   
The Natural History Museum wishes to secure the services of a Principal Contractor to undertake the exhibition fit-out, including sub-contracting the services of an AV Integrator and specialist showcase manufacturer.

milestones.description:
Leicestershire County Council is publishing this notice to provide advance information to the market regarding an upcoming procurement opportunity for the provision of Community Life Choices (CLC) Services. 
No formal market engagement has been undertaken in relation to this procurement opportunity. This notice is issued for information purposes only and is intended to provide visibility of the Council's current intentions to enable providers to undertake forward planning - this notice does not constitute a call for competition/invitation to tender.
Interested bidders should monitor Find a Tender and the ProActis portal for any future notices relating to this opportunity. 
The Council is considering the establishment of a new CLC Framework to support adults who have eligible social care needs and who require support to achieve greater independence, wellbeing and participation within their local communities. The framework is expected to continue the Council's person-centred approach, supporting people to achieve the outcomes that matter most to them whilst promoting independence and reducing, delaying or preventing the need for longer-term support.
The Council's current intention is that the framework will comprise of two lots - Lot 1: Group Activities within a defined base and out in the wider community & Lot 2: Managed Personal Assistants. 
The CLC framework will run from 07th June 2027 until 06th June 2030, with the option to extend to 06th June 2032. 
The timetable is currently anticipated to be as follows:
Publication of tender opportunity: Oct 2026
Evaluation Period (Including moderation): Nov 2026 - Feb 2027
Intention to Award (publication of UK06) & Standstill: April 2027
Mobilisation: Mid-April 2027
New Framework Commencement: June 2027
Please note that the above timetable is indicative, and LCC reserves the right, to amend the Procurement Timetable.
If you would like to have an informal chat about this opportunity please contact Katie Joondan, Lead Commissioner, Leicestershire County Council - katie.joondan@leics.gov.uk

tender.title: Supply of Motus Wave Sensors
tender.description:
Supply of Motus Wave Sensors as and when required by Met Office with one year warranty. 
This Contract shall commence on the Contract Start Date and shall remain in force for an initial period of four (4) years from the Contract Start Date (the "Initial Period"). The Contract may be extended at the end of the Initial Period for a further period of two (2) years ("Optional Extension Period") by the Met Office giving written notice of extension to the Supplier no later than 3 months prior to the expiry of the Initial Period.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
New sensors will be required to replace existing stock deemed beyond economical repair for 2027 and beyond. 
The Marine Moored Buoy network exclusively uses the Motus Wave sensor. Aanderaa no longer have a UK distributor for the Motus Wave Sensor. 
A significant amount of engineering effort has been dedicated to integrating MOTUS wave sensors into the Marine Moored Network, where they are the sole wave sensor used by the Met Office across our Moored ODAS buoy sites. Previous acceptance trials have demonstrated that MOTUS is an exceptionally accurate and reliable sensor. 
Continuity of sensor supply enables standardisation of fleet technology and provides technically identical outputs for reliable scientific comparability of readings.

tender.title: Transportation and Processing of Dry Mixed Recycling
tender.description:
The Council requires a contractor to provide the collection, haulage, sorting, processing and onward marketing/reprocessing of approximately 18,500 tonnes of Dry Mixed Recycling (DMR) per annum, collected from approximately 160,000 residential properties through the Council's kerbside recycling service. Annual tonnage is expected to increase towards approximately 20,000 tonnes per annum.
The DMR will be supplied by the Council at Federation Road Transfer Station, Burslem, Stoke-on-Trent, ST6 4HU, or an alternative Council-nominated location within North Staffordshire where required. The Contractor must provide sufficient haulage capacity to collect the material, currently approximately three loaded trailers per day, Monday to Thursday, with additional capacity to manage seasonal and Christmas peaks. The Contractor must provide and maintain the required empty trailer capacity at the Council's nominated delivery point.
The Contractor must transport the DMR to a suitably licensed and permitted processing facility, where it must be sorted and processed into recyclable material streams suitable for onward sale and reprocessing. The resulting Sorted Output Materials (SOM) must be transported to suitably licensed merchants, reprocessors or other approved end destinations.
Non-recyclable materials, contamination and process residues must be managed in accordance with the waste hierarchy, with the service designed to maximise diversion from landfill. Energy from Waste should be used for contaminants and process residues where practicable.
The Contractor must provide suitable licensed and permitted processing facilities, contingency arrangements, certified weighing facilities and full traceability of the DMR from collection through processing to its final destination. The service must include monthly reporting of tonnage, material composition, contamination, processing destinations and weighbridge information, together with waste composition analysis.
The service must be delivered in compliance with all applicable waste, environmental and permitting legislation, including the Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2011, Environmental Protection Act 1990 and Environmental Permitting Regulations 2010.
Any alternative processing or contingency arrangements required to maintain service continuity must be provided at no additional cost to the Council.
Summary:
What is required: collection, haulage, sorting, processing and marketing/reprocessing of DMR.
Amount: approximately 18,500 tonnes per year, increasing towards 20,000 tonnes.
Where/how supplied by the Council: Federation Road Transfer Station, with an alternative North Staffordshire location if required.
How the contractor must supply the service: approximately 3 loaded trailers per day, Monday-Thursday, sufficient trailer capacity, processing at licensed facilities, sorting into recyclable streams and onward delivery to licensed end destinations.
How non-recyclables are dealt with: waste hierarchy, maximum landfill diversion and EfW where practicable.
Key delivery requirements: licensed facilities, contingency, weighing, traceability and reporting
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
The Council considers a direct award to MATIQ Group Ltd to be justified under the Procurement Act 2023 on the grounds of extreme and unavoidable urgency arising from unforeseeable circumstances. The voluntary liquidation of the incumbent contractor and the loss of its principal processing facility created an immediate risk to the continuity of the Council's statutory recycling service, which could not reasonably have been foreseen and which does not allow sufficient time to conduct a competitive procurement exercise. MATIQ Group Ltd  (appointed by the  previous provider) has already demonstrated the necessary capacity, capability and compliance through existing contingency arrangements.
An 18-month term is proposed as a proportionate interim arrangement to safeguard continuity of a statutory waste collection service while the Council undertakes the necessary market assessment, governance and procurement activity for the longer-term solution, and allows greater clarity to emerge regarding the wider strategic environment in which those longer-term arrangements will operate. The period provides a realistic and controlled timeframe to develop the future procurement strategy, complete the required approvals and allow sufficient time for any subsequent provider to mobilise effectively. This approach balances the immediate statutory service requirement with the Council's obligation to achieve a robust, competitive and sustainable longer-term procurement outcome.

Supply Chain Coordination Limited (“NHS Supply Chain”) is establishing a Framework for Clinical & Sharps Waste Management. The Framework covers a wide variety of products and services. Please review the specific Lot information further down this notice regarding which products are covered under which Lot.
The Lot structure is as follows:
Lot 1: Plastic Clinical & Sharps Containers
Lot 2: Non Plastic Clinical & Sharps Containers
Lot 3: Lead Liners 
Lot 4: Sharps Pads & Associated Products
Lot 5: Services (Reusable Clinical & Sharps end to end, Waste collection & Waste Collection & recovery) 
For this tender, the following requirements will apply:   
• ISO Certification: Tenderers must have ISO 9001: 2015 or ISO 13485:2016 or Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP) certification accredited by the United Kingdom Accreditation Service (UKAS) (or international equivalent) to cover all segments of the Tenderer’s and the product’s supply chain. This should include, but not be limited to, sales, manufacturing, storage and distribution ('ISO Certification') Link for acceptable UKAS alternatives https://iaf.nu/en/accreditation-bodies/ 
• CE Certification and Declaration of Conformity certificates are required where applicable to be presented at submission stage of the tender.   
• Modern Slavery for Tenderers that have an annual turnover of at least £36 million must have a link to their modern slavery statement on their website   
• Modern Slavery Assessment Tool (MSAT) Tenderers must have a score of 41% or above within 12 months prior to the Tender Close Date and shared with NHS Supply Chain Coordination via the share function on the SRS Portal: https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/login 
• Evergreen Sustainable Supplier Assessment – Tenderers will need to have completed the assessment and achieved ‘Level One’ or above within 12 months prior to the Tender Close Date. Link for instructions and access for this assessment: https://www.england.nhs.uk/nhs-commercial/central-commercial-function-ccf/evergreen/ 
• Carbon Reduction Plan (CRP): Tenderers must have a valid CRP link on their website that meets the requirements of PPN 006 as outlined in the PPN, OR Where Supplier has no website, the CRP is provided in PDF format that meets the requirements of PPN 006 as outlined in the PPN, OR Excused in exceptional circumstances.  
• Cyber Security: If you handle patient or personal data, or provide any IT systems, services, or devices you will need to have a Cyber Security Essentials Plus Certificate.

NHS Supply Chain intends to launch a National Framework Agreement for the provision of Clinical and Sharps Waste Management, that includes the following: Clinical and Sharps Bins for single use and Accessories, Re usable Clinical and Sharps Bins Service and Accessories, Waste Management Services for Clinical and Heathcare waste, Clinical Waste Lead Liners (Radioactive Waste Containment), Sterile Single‑Use Sharps Pads & Needle Accounting Systems, Needle Disposal.
It is anticipated that in the first 12 months of the Framework Agreement the value of purchases will be circa £72,060,000 (including VAT) however this is approximate only and may vary depending on requirements of bodies purchasing under the Framework. The Framework Agreement between NHS Supply Chain and successful Tenderers will reserve the right to purchase the same or similar supplies from Tenderers not appointed to the Framework at its sole discretion.
For Goods/Services ordered via the Transacted Routes of Supply as set out in the Framework Agreement Award Pack, only the Authority will be entitled to place Orders which it will then make available for purchase by: 1) any NHS Trust; 2) any other NHS entity; 3) any government department, agency or other statutory body; and/or 4) any private sector entity active in the UK healthcare sector; and
For Goods/Services ordered via the Direct Route of Supply as set out in the Framework Agreement Award Pack, the following Participating Authorities are entitled to place Orders: 1) the Authority; 2) any NHS Trust; 3) any other NHS entity; 4) any government department, agency or other statutory body; and/or 5) any private sector entity active in the UK healthcare sector.

milestones.description:
Swindon Borough Council invites you to contribute to Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) in relation to providing Vacant Property Repairs (Voids) works to its housing stock.
The Council intends on establishing a framework of up to three contractors to deliver Vacant Property Repairs (Voids) works over an initial framework period of 24 months with an option to extend by up to 12 months. The estimated contract commencement date is 14th January 2027.
Swindon Borough Council has a housing stock of approximately 10,500 properties across the Borough plus a number of sheltered accommodation properties (if required), of which approximately 600 properties are void each year. Vacant properties may require refurbishment, general maintenance, repair and improvements to return them for re-letting on line with Swindon’s Re-let standard. The works can range from minor repairs to major capital works requiring full property renovation, depending on the age of the property and condition upon return.
Of the approximate 600 void properties each year, approximately 250 properties per year are refurbished by the Council’s in-house team.
A further circa 175 properties are refurbished by an external contractor under a term contract.
For the remaining circa 175 properties, the Council is proposing to establish a framework consisting of up to three contractors to deliver the required works on those properties and, upon completion, handed back to the Council for allocation to prospective tenants.
Details of the proposed format for call-offs is provided in the PME Questionnaire.
Information of the work types required under this framework is provided within the PME Questionnaire.
The estimated framework annual value is £2,134,490.00.
The purpose of this PME is to gain market insight into the following aspects of the project:
•	Market Interest
•	Capacity
•	Mobilisation
•	Insurances
•	Pricing
To participate in the PME, Suppliers will need to Register as a Supplier with ProContract, https://www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk , then Register an Interest before obtaining access to the PME Questionnaire. In the event of difficulties registering as a supplier, please refer to the System Administrator Proactis support team ( https://suppliersupport.proactisservicedesk.com ).
This PME exercise will close at 16:00 on 25th September 2026 and completed questionnaires are to be submitted by this date and time; following this all responses shall be reviewed by Swindon Borough Council.

tender.title: ET180 - Organ On Chip
tender.description:
LSTM and iiCON are now seeking to procure advanced Organ-on-Chip (OoC) technologies for integration into the AIR-HC facility. The technologies sought may include, but are not limited to, models incorporating tonsillar, lung and liver tissues, with preference for multi-organ-on-chip (MOoC) platforms capable of physiologically relevant inter-organ communication. The purpose of this project is to Supply Organ on Chip technology for infectious disease research at Containment level 3 / schedule 5 pathogens biosafety laboratory.  The scope of this tender includes the supply, delivery, installation and commissioning of the proposed system(s), together with any required design adaptation, packaging and shipping, user training, technical documentation, and ongoing maintenance, servicing and upgrade pathways necessary to ensure sustained cutting-edge performance within a CL3 automated environment.  
The procured technology will support both internal academic research programmes and commercial activities delivered through iiCON and the AIR-HC facility. Accordingly, LSTM seeks scalable, automation-compatible, and future-proof platforms suitable for integration into robotic workflows and capable of operating within the spatial and biosafety constraints of a high-containment laboratory. Solutions offering multi-organ capability within a compact footprint, and those designed to support expansion and increased throughput over time, will be particularly advantageous.

tender.title: 715933488 - In-Barracks Equipment Support (IBES) outputs for the Support Helicopter Force (SHF) and Commando Helicopter Force (CHF).
tender.description:
There is an enduring requirement for contracted labour and personnel support across aviation engineering, logistics information systems, airworthiness records, supply and enabling functions at RAF Odiham, RAF Benson and RNAS Yeovilton. The Authority are seeking a Contractor who shall provide suitably qualified and experienced personnel (SQEP) to supplement Service personnel and deliver the defined outputs where military capacity is constrained. This is an output-based personnel support requirement; it does not prescribe fixed posts or transfer the Authority’s responsibility for directing and assuring Defence outputs.
The requirement is informed by persistent Service workforce pressure across engineering, logistics and enabling functions. Workforce gap data may be used by the Authority to inform planning and prioritisation; however, such data is contextual only and shall not be interpreted as a fixed staffing requirement, guaranteed workload or commitment to any specific workforce construct.
The requirement supports the Authority’s need to generate, sustain and recover SUPPORT HELICOPTER FORCE  (SHF) and COMMANDO HELICOPTER FORCE  (CHF) capability in support of Defence-directed tasks, readiness commitments, force generation activity, contingency response and wider operational outputs. Delivery shall contribute to aircraft availability, maintenance throughput, logistics resilience, airworthiness assurance and safe operating outputs across the SHF and CHF enterprises.
The Contractor shall deliver support that enables the Authority to prioritise scarce engineering, logistics, supply and enabling resources against variable operational demand. Support shall remain responsive to flying programme requirements, maintenance activity, emergent tasking, readiness cycles, future capability transition and changes in workload across output groups, functions, locations and time.
The Authority does not guarantee a fixed volume of tasking. Activity assumptions, historic data and annexed output schedules are indicative and shall not be interpreted as guaranteed workload, fixed workforce demand or a prescriptive staffing schedule.

Enhancements include depot mapping, digital train preparation, incident management, engineering change control, fleet modification tracking and train software configuration management.

A change of supplier would risk significant operational disruption, duplication of costs and integration challenges associated with replacing an established business-critical system.
