tender.description:
This contract will commission an intervention and prevention Young Carers Service for Swansea, ensuring young carers and their families receive timely and appropriate support.
The commissioned provider will deliver a coordinated support offer for young carers, including assessment, safeguarding oversight, emotional and practical support, respite opportunities, youth club and group sessions, one-to-one support, school engagement, awareness raising, and links to wider partnership support. tender.title: Child Poverty Action Plan - Programme Evaluation
tender.description:
The North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) seeks to commission an external consultant to undertake an independent programme level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan 2025-2030.
The evaluation will assess the design, implementation, and impact of a complex, multi-strand programme delivered between August 2025 and March 2030. This will include directly funded activities, wider activities mobilised through the programme and selected aligned activities where appropriate and supported by the available evidence. 
The commissioned evaluation is intended as a cross-cutting programme-level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan as a whole. It is recognised that individual projects, interventions and delivery activity within the wider programme will be subject to separate monitoring, evaluation and research activity commissioned by the North East MSA or undertaken by delivery partners. 
The evaluation will synthesise evidence generated through proportionate project level evaluations (including light touch monitoring and in depth project deep dives) to provide a coherent, programme wide assessment and will not be responsible for conducting primary project-level evaluations, except where explicitly agreed. This will support strategic assurance, learning and decision making, and inform future iterations of the Action Plan and wider North East MSA and regional policy and investment decisions.
The programme-level evaluation will therefore consider both the evidence relating to individual interventions and the combined contribution of the wider programme towards the intended outcomes of the Child Poverty Action Plan.
The programme‑level evaluation will also seek to determine the degree to which reducing child poverty has been embedded as a cross-cutting theme across North East MSA activity, and that of partners. This will include examining how the Child Poverty Reduction Unit and the regional Child Poverty Action Plan have influenced strategic priorities, programme and project design, funding and delivery decisions, and whether they have contributed to changes in policies, practices and activities beyond those directly funded through the programme.

This Open Framework is defined as a procurement where any supplier who feels they meet the requirements in the specification can submit a bid.  
It's a single stage process with no prequalification requirements

Suppliers will be informed of the initial winning bidders and given relevant feedback.  
After the initial period of 2 years the framework competition will re-open and existing framework suppliers can resubmit a new bid or maintain their original bid. Due to the value, call-offs under this agreement will be done with framework providers via purchase order. 
Call-offs will be assigned based on Service User choice, where a Service User has no preference or cannot make a decision, work will be assigned in Framework rank order.

tender.title: Undercliffs NNR Humble Glades Holm Oak felling
tender.description:
The contractor is required to carry out safe felling and removal of all spray marked trees in the project area, the Humble Glades. This is the equivalent of approximately 80 medium-size trees, approximately 40m3 of timber, although the actual number of trees may be higher. There are a small number of Turkey Oak and Pine that are included in the felling contract but 90% of the trees are Holm Oak. The trees need to be safely felled and then processed. The majority of the timber felled needs to be burnt on site following instructions from Natural England concerning location and number of firesites. The cut stumps of all felled trees need to be treated with a Glyphosate based herbicide to prevent re-growth.
The Axmouth to Lyme Regis Undercliffs NNR is a remote and wild coastal landslip. The worksite is located a 20-30 minute walk from the nearest vehicle access. The terrain across the NNR includes steep, uneven and sometimes difficult ground. The worksite is similar in terrain, on uneven, challenging and sometimes steep ground.
Contractors will be required to hold and submit relevant chainsaw, herbicide and first aid certification, including felling and processing of medium-size trees (380mm to 760mm / up to twice bar length). Contractors must wear all relevant PPE at all times. No lone working at any time. The contractor must hold and submit a copy of their public liability insurance.
It is a requirement that contractors undertake a site visit prior to submitting a tender or quote unless they are already familiar with the site. This can be arranged with Natural England please contact tom.sunderland@naturalengland.org.uk .
A thorough Risk Assessment will need to be drawn up and agreed with Natural England before any work starts.

tender.procurementMethodRationale:
This Direct Award to a single supplier is justified on the grounds set out under Paragraph 6 of Schedule 5 of Procurement Act 2023 where the following conditions are met in relation to the public contract.
Schedule 5, Paragraph 6:
The following conditions are met in relation to the public contract-
(a) due to an absence of competition for technical reasons, only a particular supplier can supply the goods, services or works required, and
(b) there are no reasonable alternatives to those goods, services or works.
The Direct Award Contract approach is standard within the sector currently as Bloomberg Finance LP is a sole supplier of Bloomberg Professional Software.  This is the main financial trading software used globally and is the most commonly used with Higher Education on related programmes.  
All of UUBS Finance programmes include integrated learning and assessment strategies linked to Bloomberg software, whilst the University also provides the Bloomberg Market Concept certification within academic and professional programmes (this is only available with the use of this software).  The software is also essential in terms of the programme developmental process in terms of FinTech.
It would be detrimental to the University's Finance programmes at all levels, including student student recruitment, if the University no longer had access to Bloomberg software as it is integral to the delivery of these programmes.  Related academic staff have been trained on the software and utilise it heavily within teaching and marketing activities to Schools.
Therefore, due to the above reasons, a DAC has been chosen as a compliant route to market.

tender.title: Control Software
tender.description: For this project We have 6 modules. Each module is made up of 3 stages. These stages are (1) an x-y stage, (2) a tilt goniometric stage, and (3) rotational stage. The links to these stages and the control box can be seen in the attached supporting document. The difference between our stages and the COTS stages is that each stage has a different motor to the COTS item (integrated 485 bus-type closed-loop stepper driver, IRS42E-K02, manual available). All modules are controlled via a single controller box. The controller box has power and user instructions from control software (via RS232 to USB cable) as inputs and has six output cables, each connected to one of the modules (RS232 to RS232). Each output cable is limited to 2m length. The cable from the controller connects to the bottom most stage of the module, that is the x-stage. The x-stage is then connected to the y-stage via a RS232 cable. The y-stage is connected to the goniometric stage via a RS232 cable. Finally, the goniometric stage is connected to the rotational stage via a RS232 cable. In this way, a controller with 6 outputs controls 6x4=24 motors. This setup is shown in the diagram and a picture of a single module is also provided on the attached supporting document. The control signal is sent via the control box to the desired module. If the control signal is not for the x-stage, the control signal is passed up the chain, and so on. We need the control software to interface with our existing hardware to control the 6 modules. The solution could interface with the existing control box, or alternatively provide a new controller to interface with the 6 modules. The requirements above are for the software/control of the 6 modules.

renewal.description:
1 x 12 month optional extensions.
Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) is the process in which the structure and responsibilities of local authorities are reconfigured. The Government has set out plans to move away from the current two-tier system of district and county councils in England, which is relevant to Cambridgeshire County Council, the five district councils in the county (Cambridge City Council, East Cambridgeshire District Council, Fenland District Council, Huntingdonshire District Council and South Cambridgeshire District Council), and Peterborough City Council as a neighbouring unitary council.  The Government has not decided when (or if) the current seven councils in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough will be reorganised and replaced with a one tier system, resulting in separate county, city and district councils no longer existing.  A one tier system will mean residents will access all services through unitary council(s). At this stage, no decisions have been made on how many unitary councils will cover the county and which geographical areas they will cover.  Throughout the LGR process, the Authority's focus will remain on delivering essential services across Peterborough. 
Accordingly, changes may occur during the term of the contract, and although contracts are likely to transfer to any new unitary authorities by statutory instrument or by agreement on LGR, the contract may need to be amended to reflect the new geographical, financial and contract scope.  Therefore, to ensure the contract may adapt upon implementation of LGR and modify to reflect the implications of LGR, we state within this procurement documentation of the intention to rely on Section 74(1)(a) and Schedule 8(1) of the Procurement Act 2023 to permit modification of the of the contract (if modification is considered necessary), to reflect new geographical, financial and contract scope accordingly.  Please note we cannot precisely confirm any modification, if any, to the geographical, financial and contract scope at this stage, and any proposed modification.  Any contract modification shall be in accordance with clause 28 and clause 32.5.2(c) of the contract.

tender.description:
Ladygrove Park is a well-used public open space located within the Ladygrove area of Didcot, comprising approximately 29 acres of accessible green space. The park provides a range of recreational facilities for residents and visitors, including:
•
Extensive public open grassed areas
•
Outdoor sports facilities
The project seeks to maximise the use of currently underutilised landscaped mounds within the play area to create an engaging, adventurous and inclusive play environment for children, primarily aimed at those aged between 5 and 11 years. Tenderers are encouraged to develop innovative design proposals that incorporate these existing landforms and create a cohesive play experience by linking the mounds where appropriate.
As part of the overall design, contractors should consider the relocation of the existing multi-play unit to higher ground within the play area. The current location is susceptible to seasonal flooding during the winter months, and proposals should demonstrate how relocating this equipment could improve its long-term usability and accessibility.
The Council invites tenderers to submit their own design concepts, making imaginative use of features such as, but not limited to:
•
Tunnels
•
Bridges
•
Slides
•
Climbing elements
•
Accessible and inclusive play features
•
Natural play opportunities
The proposed design should complement the existing playground while significantly enhancing the quality, variety and accessibility of the play experience. The Council wishes to create an attractive destination that encourages active, imaginative and inclusive play, supporting the cognitive, physical, social and emotional development of children and young people.
The existing play equipment is over 25 years old and, whilst remaining serviceable, the Council is seeking to modernise the play provision to better meet the needs of the local community and to provide facilities comparable in quality to those available at Edmonds Park.
The available project budget is currently £40,000. The Council is actively seeking additional external funding and, if successful, anticipates increasing the total project value to approximately £100,000. Subject to successful funding, the anticipated allocation is:
•
Approximately £80,000 for the design, supply and installation of new play equipment.
•
Approximately £20,000 for the relocation of the existing multi-play unit and the possible installation of an accessible see-saw, utilising the existing accessible infrastructure where appropriate.
Tenderers should therefore identify which elements of their proposal could be delivered within the confirmed budget and which additional enhancements could be incorporated should further funding become available.
This project needs to ensure full compliance with all Playground Regulations - specifically EN1176, and BS7188 and EN1177 for surfacing.
Didcot Town Council prefer to work with companies who sources their equipment from the United Kingdom, so there are less issues with delays for replacement parts.
•
A dedicated children's play area
Within the existing playground are two landscaped mounds that are currently underutilised and do not accommodate any play features.
As part of its ongoing commitment to enhancing community recreation and play opportunities, Didcot Town Council's Environment & Climate Committee has identified these mounds as suitable locations for additional play equipment. The Council is therefore seeking proposals for the design, supply and installation of play equipment that makes effective use of these features, enhances the existing play provision, and provides engaging, inclusive and high-quality play opportunities for children and young people.

tender.title: Adult Primary Care Continence
tender.description:
This contract has been awarded to Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust under Direct Award Process A of the Provider Selection Regime. The specialist urogynaecology physiotherapy service forms an integrated element of the wider Primary Care Continence Service delivered to the Cheshire West population and is clinically interdependent with the existing continence pathway operating across the West Cheshire Health Collaborative. The service requires direct integration with the established multidisciplinary continence team, shared clinical pathways, referral and triage arrangements, clinical governance processes and collaborative working arrangements that are already in place between the Provider and Cheshire and Wirral Partnership NHS Foundation Trust.
The service is not a standalone physiotherapy service that can be separated from the wider continence pathway without creating fragmentation of care, duplication of processes and disruption to patient management. Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is the only provider currently embedded within, and able to deliver the specialist physiotherapy component as part of, the existing integrated continence model across the West Cheshire Health Collaborative. Continuation of the existing arrangement ensures safe and effective patient care, maintains pathway integration and avoids disruption to patients accessing specialist continence services.
The service relies upon established clinical relationships, referral pathways, governance arrangements and multidisciplinary working practices that have been developed as part of the West Cheshire Health Collaborative model and cannot reasonably be replicated by an alternative provider without fundamental redesign of the service pathway.

The Provider has a proven track record of delivering the specialist physiotherapy element of the Primary Care Continence Service and has the necessary clinical infrastructure, governance systems, operational resources and experience to ensure safe, effective and sustainable service delivery for the Cheshire West population.

tender.title: Supply of HLA Sequencing Systems
tender.description:
NHS Blood & Transplant (NHSBT) Histocompatibility & Immunogenetics function intends to undertake a Procurement Act 2023 tender exercise for the supply of HLA sequencing systems.
Histocompatibility & Immunogenetics (H&I) is a strategic business function of NHSBT, providing testing and support in transplantation, specialised transfusion including the supply of selected blood products, immunogenetics, platelet and granulocyte immunology.
Services are supplied through a national network of six laboratories across England. Building on our strengths as a national provider, NHSBT’s strategic aim is for its diagnostic services to become the preferred provider and supplier of choice for these services in the NHS in England. We would like to work with future suppliers to realise this ambition and to perform HLA typing in an efficient, timely and cost-effective manner to meet the demands and expectations of our customers and the patients we serve.
Prior to commencing a formal procurement process and to help inform our strategy, NHSBT is seeking to engage with suppliers of commercially available HLA sequencing systems. Our current contract ends in August 2028 and NHSBT would like to improve our knowledge of all current and future systems available in the marketplace. This will aid identification of opportunities and gauge market interest in this field.
We require HLA typing systems to cover the following:
· Allelic Test Kits SHOULD detect and uniquely identify all alleles of the HLA-A, B, C, DRB1, DRB3/4/5, DQA1, DQB1, DPA1 and DPB1 loci at the level of resolution that additionally defines the third field according to WHO nomenclature by at least resolving all ambiguities resulting from: (1) polymorphisms located within the exons coding for HLA class I and class II proteins and (2) that encompass a null allele wherever the polymorphism is located.
· The optimal solution SHOULD define fourth field level resolution.
· We are not restricting which sequencing platform the allelic test kits are compatible with, however HLA typing should be completed within 72 hours of the start of the process.
NB: Procurement of the above systems may be managed by individual tenders.
It is NHSBT's intention to hold pre-procurement engagement meetings the week of 21OCT2026 to 23OCT2026 these will be held remotely, the date to be confirmed. To enable NHSBT to finalise arrangements (e.g. send meeting details and agree time slots) for the supplier engagement meetings, interested organisations are required to send an expression of interest via email to coco.otiotio@nhsbt.nhs.uk by no later than 17:00 hrs (GMT) on 09OCT2026. This should include a list of your potential attendees and a brief overview (or a website link) of the Goods / Services which might be offered. Please include options, if available, to offer a managed service contract.
No business whatsoever is guaranteed under any resulting framework agreement or contract, and there is no guarantee that any framework agreement or contract will be put in place in relation to this notice. No compensation etc. will be paid if a tender or resulting framework agreement is withdrawn for any reason. Bidders should take part in this process only on the basis that they fully understand and accept this position.
It should be noted that this procurement exercise may allow other Health authorities to utilise any contracts/ framework agreements awarded.

tender.title: Rough Sleeping Rapid Assessment Hub & Outreach / InReach Service
tender.description:
Southend-on-Sea City Council has awarded a contract for the provision of a Rough Sleeping Rapid Assessment Hub and Outreach/Inreach Service, funded through the Government's Rough Sleeping Initiative (RSI).
The service will provide a minimum 12-bed supported Rapid Assessment Hub for individuals sleeping rough or at risk of rough sleeping, together with an outreach and in reach function to identify, engage and support rough sleepers into accommodation and appropriate services.
The service includes assessment, housing-related support, partnership working, safeguarding, referral management, and the coordination of move-on pathways to help prevent a return to rough sleeping and contribute to the Council's objectives of reducing homelessness and rough sleeping across the city
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
Southend-on-Sea City Council proposes a direct award to HARP (Homeless Action Resource Project) for the continued provision of the Rough Sleeping Rapid Assessment Hub and Outreach /Inreach Service, valued at £352,710.24 excluding VAT.
The existing contract, originally awarded through a compliant competitive procurement process in 2022, expired on 31 March 2026 following the exercise of the available extension. Due to the late confirmation of ongoing funding, there was insufficient time to undertake and complete a new procurement before contract expiry.
HARP has continued to deliver the service to prevent disruption to critical homelessness and rough sleeping support. The proposed award will regularise the current position and provide an interim arrangement until 31 March 2027, allowing sufficient time to undertake a compliant procurement for the long-term service.
The direct award is necessary to ensure continuity of a critical service for vulnerable residents, maintain the Council's homelessness responsibilities, and avoid disruption to
accommodation, outreach, safeguarding and support provision. The arrangement represents value for money as services will continue on the same terms and pricing established through the 2022 competitive tender process.
Without this award, there is a significant risk of service interruption and the Council being unable to maintain essential rough sleeping and homelessness support services.
The contract value associated with this transparency notice accounts for the retrospective services provided by HARP from 31 March 2026 to date, as well as the future contract value up to the expiry date of 31 March 2027.

tender.title: National Parking Platform
tender.description:
Guildford Borough Council intends to join the National Parking Platform (NPP), a not-for-profit, government-backed initiative designed to modernise and simplify parking payments across participating local authorities. The NPP provides an open and interoperable platform that enables multiple parking service providers to connect to a single national parking ecosystem, allowing motorists to use their preferred parking application when paying for parking rather than being restricted to a single provider.
Through integration with the NPP, the Council will offer users greater choice, improved accessibility, and a more consistent customer experience across participating locations. The platform operates through a transaction-fee funding model and provides a centralised mechanism through which multiple approved parking service providers can facilitate parking payments on behalf of the Council.
As part of the service, participating providers will collect parking charges, undertake transaction processing and monthly reconciliations, and remit all parking revenue due to the Council in accordance with the agreed operating and settlement arrangements. The solution supports improved interoperability within the parking sector while maintaining the Council's control over parking tariffs and revenue.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
This direct award is made pursuant to Section 41 and Schedule 5, Paragraph 6 of the Procurement Act 2023. The contracting authority has determined that competition is absent for technical reasons (Schedule 5, Paragraph 6(a)) and that no reasonable alternative or substitute exists (Schedule 5, Paragraph 6(b))
These conditions are satisfied because:
(a) The National Parking Platform Ltd is the only supplier of a unique multivendor cashless parking solution, which is currently able to supply the critical service of aggregating service providers so as to enable users of a parking operator's facilities to pay for parking with a wide range of parking apps.
(b) National Parking Platform Ltd holds exclusive rights to operate and develop the Platform, which was originally commissioned by the Department for Transport. No other supplier has access to this public asset grant.
(c) The NPP operates as a central, shared interoperability platform with:
•	A single, governed technical integration layer enabling approved parking service providers to connect
•	Controlled onboarding, certification, and access arrangements managed by NPP
•	A defined ecosystem where authorities must connect via the platform to enable interoperability
•	No individual supplier can independently replicate or provide:
•	Access to the NPP integration layer
•	The ability to onboard multiple payment providers within a nationally recognised interoperability framework
•	The same level of cross-authority interoperability
d) The requirement to integrate with the NPP does not artificially narrow competition because:
•	The NPP is designed as an open, non-exclusive platform enabling multiple parking service providers to participate
•	Competition is preserved at the payment provider level, where multiple suppliers can operate via the NPP
•	The Authority is not selecting a single downstream provider but enabling a competitive marketplace of providers
•	The specification reflects a genuine operational need for interoperability, not a preference for a specific supplier
•	Therefore, the direct award relates only to the core interoperability platform, while maintaining competition in the wider service ecosystem.

tender.title: Play Equipment at Ladygrove Park, Didcot
tender.description:
Ladygrove Park is a well-used public open space located within the Ladygrove area of Didcot, comprising approximately 29 acres of accessible green space. The park provides a range of recreational facilities for residents and visitors, including:
•
Extensive public open grassed areas
•
Outdoor sports facilities
The project seeks to maximise the use of currently underutilised landscaped mounds within the play area to create an engaging, adventurous and inclusive play environment for children, primarily aimed at those aged between 5 and 11 years. Tenderers are encouraged to develop innovative design proposals that incorporate these existing landforms and create a cohesive play experience by linking the mounds where appropriate.
As part of the overall design, contractors should consider the relocation of the existing multi-play unit to higher ground within the play area. The current location is susceptible to seasonal flooding during the winter months, and proposals should demonstrate how relocating this equipment could improve its long-term usability and accessibility.
The Council invites tenderers to submit their own design concepts, making imaginative use of features such as, but not limited to:
•
Tunnels
•
Bridges
•
Slides
•
Climbing elements
•
Accessible and inclusive play features
•
Natural play opportunities
The proposed design should complement the existing playground while significantly enhancing the quality, variety and accessibility of the play experience. The Council wishes to create an attractive destination that encourages active, imaginative and inclusive play, supporting the cognitive, physical, social and emotional development of children and young people.
The existing play equipment is over 25 years old and, whilst remaining serviceable, the Council is seeking to modernise the play provision to better meet the needs of the local community and to provide facilities comparable in quality to those available at Edmonds Park.
The available project budget is currently £40,000. The Council is actively seeking additional external funding and, if successful, anticipates increasing the total project value to approximately £100,000. Subject to successful funding, the anticipated allocation is:
•
Approximately £80,000 for the design, supply and installation of new play equipment.
•
Approximately £20,000 for the relocation of the existing multi-play unit and the possible installation of an accessible see-saw, utilising the existing accessible infrastructure where appropriate.
Tenderers should therefore identify which elements of their proposal could be delivered within the confirmed budget and which additional enhancements could be incorporated should further funding become available.
This project needs to ensure full compliance with all Playground Regulations - specifically EN1176, and BS7188 and EN1177 for surfacing.
Didcot Town Council prefer to work with companies who sources their equipment from the United Kingdom, so there are less issues with delays for replacement parts.
•
A dedicated children's play area
Within the existing playground are two landscaped mounds that are currently underutilised and do not accommodate any play features.
As part of its ongoing commitment to enhancing community recreation and play opportunities, Didcot Town Council's Environment & Climate Committee has identified these mounds as suitable locations for additional play equipment. tender.title: CEFAS26-11 Framework for Next Generation Sequencing Services
tender.description:
Cefas are seeking to establish a Framework for the provision of Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) services, for a variety of NGS analyses methods, to support the delivery of numerous and varied research programmes that are utilising genomics.
The framework is split into 4 Lots and Suppliers can bid for any number of Lots. Cefas intends to award up to 5 Contracts for each Lot, based on Suppliers meeting the required technical and pricing evaluation criteria. Cefas will then call-off from the framework for individual project requirements, as set out in the full Specification of Requirement document in the Bidder Pack. If a Supplier is awarded multiple Lots, one Contract will be awarded to cover the relevant Lots.
The Contract implementation is expected to start in August 2026 for a period of 3 years with the option to extend for 2 further periods of 12 months each.
Prices will be fixed for the initial 3 year period of the Contract. Prices may then be increased on an annual basis if the Contract is extended, in line with CPI.
Lot 1 - Targeted Sequencing
Suppliers will deliver targeted sequencing analyses, such as:
• Amplicon sequencing and metabarcoding, utilising mainly 16S, 18S, COI and ITS markers, but also other custom primers may be required on an ad-hoc basis.
• Library enrichment, such as bait capture/hybrid probe capture techniques.
Lot 2 - Whole Genome
Suppliers will deliver whole genome, metagenomic and transcriptomic sequencing, in applications such as:
• Whole genome/metagenomic sequencing for microbial diversity, microbiome analysis, species identification, pathogen detection, genome assembly, AMR screening, population genetics.
• Transcriptomic/single-cell/spatial transcriptomic sequencing for host-pathogen interactions, functional annotation/classification, metabolic pathways, gene expression.
Lot 3 - Long-Read Sequencing
Suppliers will provide long-read sequencing analysis, using either PacBio or Oxford Nanopore Technologies. This may be for several different applications, mainly studies of:
• Microbial diversity, microbiome analysis, species identification, pathogen detection
• Whole-genome assembly, AMR screening, population genetics
• Nanopore-specific - Methylation sequencing, epigenetics
Lot 4 - Ad-Hoc Requirements
Suppliers will ad-hoc requests, i.e. those that do not fit in the prior lot categories. This would most likely be utilised when a unique/proprietary technology or analysis is required, such as RAD-Seq, that Cefas cannot undertake in-house.
Specifics would be detailed in the individual project request via the call-off process, which will be a mini-competition process as set out in Appendix 4.

tender.title: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit
tender.description:
The National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) will be for NHS-funded care in England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Jersey (inclusion of other devolved nations/Crown dependencies is yet to be determined and will be detailed within the tender documentation). 
The initial contract is anticipated to be for a period of 3 years, at a maximum total budget of up to £ 951,168.00 excl VAT and £1,141,401.00 with VAT. Bids exceeding this limit will be rejected. Due to the unknowns in advance of holding the premarket engagement session, it is currently expected that the extension value will be a 2-year pro rata of the core 3-year funding, estimated at £634,112.00 excluding VAT.  
There is potential to include other Devolved Nations and/or Crown Dependencies, and aspirational measures (which will be defined in the service specification).
The role of a national clinical audit is to stimulate healthcare improvement through the provision of timely and high-quality information on the organisation, delivery and outcomes of healthcare, together with tools and support to enable healthcare providers and other audiences to make best use of this information. Outcomes are benchmarked against national guidance and standards e.g. quality standards from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), and those from other established professional and patient sources. Successful national audits are those where the individuals providing the data can also improve the system, and there is a shared understanding of what good care looks like. 
The National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) was established in 2011 and has been delivered by the Royal College of Anaesthetists (RCoA) - https://www.nela.org.uk/  
 The overarching aim of this audit is to stimulate improvements in care for patients undergoing and not undergoing emergency laparotomy through the provision of high-quality comparative data from all providers of emergency laparotomy by measuring and reporting variations in quality of care and patient outcomes. During this contract period, the successful tenderer will need to build on the achievements of the audit to date and enhance the ability for the audit to be used for healthcare improvement by engaging with clinicians, patients and commissioners (both local and national) and regional networks.  
Successful national audits are those where the individuals providing the data are also in a position to improve the system, and where there is a shared understanding of what good care looks like. Data is most useful locally for healthcare improvement when its provision to clinical teams is timely, the data is refreshed regularly, and appropriate tools, support and guidance accompany the data outputs. The intent is for all of these features to be implemented and improved during the period of this future contract.
Develop a robust, high-quality audit designed around key quality metrics likely to best support local and national quality improvement 
Detect, describe and help reduce unwarranted clinical variation by systematically benchmarking performance, identifying outliers, and supporting services to understand variation in outcomes, processes and experience 
Achieve, articulate and maintain close alignment with relevant NICE national guidance and quality standards throughout the audit, as appropriate 
Enable healthcare quality improvements through the provision of timely, high-quality data that compares providers of healthcare, and comprises an integrated mixture of named Trust or Health Board, Integrated Care System (ICS), multi-disciplinary team, possibly consultant or clinical team level and other levels of reporting 
Engage patients, carers and the public in a meaningful way, achieving a strong patient voice which informs and contributes to the design, functioning, outputs and direction of the audit 
Consider the value and feasibility of linking data at an individual patient level to other relevant national datasets either from the outset or in the future, and plan for these linkages from the inception of the contract 
Ensure robust methodological and statistical input at all stages of the audit 
Identify from the outset the full range of audiences for the reports and other audit outputs, and plan and tailor them accordingly.
By way of example, the current contract specification includes the following anticipated benefits of the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit: 
National benchmarking to highlight unwarranted variation between providers 
Sustained reduction in 30-day mortality and postoperative complications through systematic performance monitoring against national standards 
Reduced length of hospital stay, supporting faster recovery and improved patient flow 
Increased delivery of time-critical interventions (e.g. antibiotics for sepsis, timely access to theatre), improving survival and outcomes 
Enhanced care for high-risk and frail patients, including improved peri-operative specialist input 
Shift from retrospective reporting to near real-time data and interactive dashboards 
Improved insight for regulators, commissioners and systems (ICSs) through consistent performance data 
Systematic identification and management of outliers and ‘cause for concern’, enabling early intervention 
Standardised performance metrics aligned with NICE and other national guidance 
Provide audit results in a timely, accessible and meaningful manner to support healthcare quality improvement, minimising the reporting delay and providing continual access to each unit for their own data 
Utilise strong and effective project and programme management to deliver audit outputs on time and within budget 
Develop and maintain strong engagement with local clinicians, networks, commissioners, patients and their families and carers and charity and community support groups to drive improvements in services 
Embedded healthcare improvement plans with measurable objectives and ongoing impact evaluation 
Support for coordinated improvement across the entire emergency laparotomy pathway 
Increased use of routine data and data linkage to reduce manual data collection burden 
Improved data completeness, quality and efficiency, supporting robust analysis and decision-making 
Systematic assessment of inequalities in access, care and outcomes 
Support for national and local priorities to reduce inequalities and promote parity of care 
Active involvement of patients, carers and the public in audit design, outputs and improvement priorities 
Flexibility to expand scope (e.g. non-operative pathways, wider geographies including devolved nations and Crown Dependencies) 
Designed to evolve with emerging evidence and service models 
  Further details of the existing audit can be found at: https://www.nela.org.uk/

tender.title: The Provision and Maintenance of Two Mass Spectrometry systems
tender.description:
The MHRA has a requirement to award a contract for The Provision and Maintenance of Two Mass Spectrometry systems to one Tenderer as replacements of two Triple Quad Mass Spectrometers (s/n TQH-Q1-0526 and TQH-Q1-0525) for quantification and characterisation of biological medicine standards, including influenza, and to support counterfeit and sub-potent medicine characterisation. These systems are to be purchased with service maintenance and any bespoke consumables required to run the systems as follows:
System 1. A high-resolution mass spectrometer coupled with a low flow liquid chromatography (LC) system (hereinafter referred to as a “high resolution mass spectrometry system” or “HRMS system”). The system should include all the instrumentation and software to allow qualitative and quantitative analysis of samples in a wide range of complex biological matrices in the areas of proteomics, intact protein analysis, biopharmaceutical characterisation, e.g. multi-attribute monitoring of therapeutic antibodies, post-translational modifications and small molecules/metabolomics as well as glycoproteins and oligonucleotides (OGNs).
System 2. A triple quadrupole mass spectrometer coupled with an ultra-high performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) (hereinafter referred to as a “triple quad MS system”). The system should include all the instrumentation and software to allow for high throughput targeted quantitative analysis across biopharma, clinical and small molecule applications, supporting large SRM/MRM panels.

Provides a single source of truth for employee data across all schools and the Trust's central team.
Reduces administrative workloads and manual processing.
Ensures accurate, timely payroll with all third-party submissions completed by the provider, including HMRC, pension providers, and statutory bodies.
Supports workforce planning, reporting, and strategic oversight at Trust level.
Offers excellent employee and manager self-service.
Ensures data security, GDPR compliance, and UK-based hosting.
Scope of software and services
The software will include:
General HR system of record (SoR)
Absence and attendance management functionality, which will link to occupational sickness scheme requirements
Time and expenses (the functionality for employees to log additional hours and expenses, which would only be approved at managerial level)
Organisation structure
Employee Self Service
Manager Self Service
People Analytics
A fully managed payroll and pension service
The Trust would not be procuring the functionality below in the first instance but may consider doing at a later date. These are, therefore, 'desirable' rather than 'essential':
Integrated applicant tracking and onboarding functionality
Performance management and appraisal functionality
Case management functionality
The service provision will include:
Fully managed payroll services
Fully managed pensions services
Solution hosting
Requirements
Our requirements (functional and non-functional) have been listed and are provided in an Excel sheet along with this document.

Additionally, please provide a high level project plan to demonstrate the timescales that your solution could be deployed in and a copy of your customer support service-level agreement (SLA). Finally, short-listed providers will be required to complete the Trust's data protection impact assessment (DPIA).

tender.description: Lot 1: Supported housing for men who are homeless, rough sleeping, at risk of rough sleeping or at risk of repeat homelessness, and who require accommodation and housing-related support to obtain, sustain and progress from accommodation. The Service will provide a flexible mix of dispersed and scheme-based accommodation, with trauma-informed, strengths-based support that promotes stability, independence and successful move-on into settled housing. The Service will provide safe, dispersed, single occupancy accommodation with flexible, trauma-informed and inclusive support, helping people build independence and move on successfully into settled housing. Lot 3: The Service will provide safe, suitable accommodation and flexible housing-related support for people experiencing repeated homelessness, severe multiple disadvantage and high housing-related support needs. The service will focus on stabilisation, sustainment of accommodation, access to wider support, independence and move on to settled housing.

tender.title: Hazardous Waste Collection & Disposal Services at Household Hazardous Waste Events and Incidental Hazardous Waste
tender.description:
Norfolk County Council, as a Waste Disposal Authority, is required by the Environmental Protection Act 1990, section 51, to provide reasonably accessible sites for the free disposal of household waste by its residents. 
The seven District, Borough and City councils in Norfolk as Waste Collection Authorities have a statutory duty to provide a collection service for household hazardous waste. In terms of hazardous waste disposal, Norfolk County Council has met this obligation by holding 'Hazardous Waste Events' on set weekends, at specific Recycling Centres (RC). Such events have been held annually since 2003. This is an opportunity for householders to deposit hazardous waste such as domestic paint and thinners, pesticides, fertilisers, fire extinguishers and household cleaning products. 
Visitor numbers across the network of RCs for 2025 was over 910,000.  Many households  therefore visit the Household Hazardous Waste Days (HHWD) to dispose of such material. There were over 12, 495 visitors to the 14 HHWD in 2025 (two events).
The HHWD take place during dedicated weekends where an area of the participating RC is designated to receive household hazardous waste. Whilst the RC is normally only open 9am - 4pm, for the purposes of the HHWD, RC will have extended opening hours of 8am to 4pm.  All visits to the RCs are made via a booking system. Without a valid booking, members of the public will be refused entry.
These events are primarily designed for the receiving of hazardous waste, and therefore normal waste is restricted. The site Contractor will still be making bin collections and exchanges, but these are kept to a minimum.  Any HGV movements at Hempton RC ONLY will require it to be closed for safety reasons. Norfolk's service standard is that these exchanges must not exceed 30 minutes. Any closures will be kept to a minimum.
In addition to the hazardous waste events, the Council has a responsibility to respond to unplanned incidents where hazardous waste arises due to, for example, small or larger scale fly tipping or coastal pollution incidents, ensuring that appropriate arrangements are made for the treatment or disposal of the waste.

tender.procurementMethodRationale:
CMAL intends to award a contract for Designer and Principal Designer services in connection with the Ardrossan Harbour Redevelopment Project following a further competition conducted under Lot 7 of the Scotland Excel Engineering and Technical Consultancy Framework Agreement (Ref. 1025).
A capability and capacity assessment was undertaken across suppliers appointed to the relevant Framework lot. Suppliers assessed as capable of delivering the requirement were invited to participate in a further competition through PCS-Tender. Tenders were evaluated in accordance with the published award criteria and weightings, and Wallace Stone achieved the highest overall score and has been identified as the preferred bidder.
CMAL is procuring these services in connection with activities that fall within the scope of the Utilities Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2016 ("UCR"). The Scotland Excel Framework was established under the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015 ("PCR"). CMAL has obtained legal advice regarding the use of the Framework for this requirement.
CMAL considers that:
- CMAL is entitled to access and use the Framework as an authorised user;
- the services required fall within the scope of the Framework and the relevant lot;
- the Framework was established through a transparent and competitive procurement process; and
- the further competition has provided a fair and competitive opportunity to capable Framework suppliers.
CMAL acknowledges that use of a Framework established under PCR for a requirement falling within UCR may give rise to an arguable technical procurement risk. However, having regard to the competitive process used to establish the Framework, CMAL's entitlement to use it, the scope alignment of the services, and the competitive further competition undertaken, CMAL considers there to be a reasonable and proportionate basis for proceeding with the proposed award.
CMAL is therefore publishing this VEAT notice in the interests of transparency and intends to conclude the contract following expiry of a voluntary standstill period, provided no successful challenge is received.

tender.title: HAC6148 Comprehensive Diagnostic of Health and Adult Social Care
tender.description: The London Borough of Tower Hamlets has experienced sustained and accelerating growth in adult social care demand for and access to care and support across both working age adults and the older population. Complexity of needs and the unit cost of care have also increased. These trends are reinforced by wider demographic pressures, with the borough’s population expected to rise to 381,188 by 2030, and the number of residents aged 75+ forecasted to increase by 56% by 2045. The financial implications of this trajectory are amplified by the borough’s exceptionally high levels of income deprivation among older adults—61.5% live in income deprivation, the highest proportion in England, driving significantly higher reliance on council funded care. As a result, we already commission the second highest number of care packages per head of population aged 65+ nationally and the third most community care packages in London per head of population aged 65+. • To produce a business case and delivery plan for transformation of ASC, which identifies opportunities to support the directorate in achieving improved outcomes for residents, and a reduction in spend on specific pathways, ensuring we continue to meet the eligible care needs of our residents and deliver on our statutory duties whilst ensuring we are resilient to future increase in demand

tender.title: Live Fire Training Unit
tender.description:
East Sussex Fire Authority (ESFA) on behalf of East Sussex Fire and Rescue Service require to replace their Live Fire Training Building situated on our Training Centre site in Maresfield East Sussex.
This exercise is being created to replace the previous exercise called Live Fire Training Building (but with the same reference number) as we ran into portal constraints that blocked this being an open tender open to all new interested parties. To do so we had to cease the previous exercise and commence a new one.
Our intention is to replace essentially what we have now on a like for like basis but taking into account some design changes identified that will improve both flexibility in use and reduce the impact we have on the environment. We have a fairly clear idea of what we want, and that we can afford it, and believe we have a basic understanding of who might be able to supply what we require in a fairly small niche market. However, the aim of this document is to allow the market to confirm, or otherwise, our assumptions and for us to gather some information that will allow us to prepare an equitable tender that any capable supplier could bid for.  As well as establishing capable suppliers we are very keen to establish whether this can be achieved as a single supplier integrated project, or not.
Whilst we may consider alternative innovative approaches, we believe that a steel framed metal structure or container-based solution is likely to be all that we can afford and of which, we have a lot of experience being the basis of the current unit.
This Tender will be managed electronically via the In-Tend Portal. It can be reached via:	https://sell2.in-tend.co.uk/blpd/home
Contractors need to be registered to use the portal and registered against us as a Contracting Entity, but registration is free and further information on how this is achieved, can be found at:	
https://sell2.in-tend.co.uk/blpd/register
If you are unsure about your company's registration status, or have problems accessing the tender on the portal, please contact In-Tend Portals support at:	https://in-tend.co.uk/contact-us/
If you have any difficulties with the In-Tend Portal that you are unable to resolve through the Sell2UK helpdesk, please email procurement@esfrs.org.  
UK2 PME was previously completed via a separate exercise - https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/Notice/072670-2025

tender.title: Compassionate Birmingham Expert Support and Delivery
tender.description:
Birmingham City Council (the Council) is seeking to appoint an organisation for the provision of Compassionate Birmingham workstream, which is a core delivery of the Birmingham Ageing Well Strategy and the continued delivery of our Compassionate Birmingham commitment.
Compassionate Birmingham is the umbrella term given to a series of organisations that work to deliver better services and support for people who are dying, bereaved, grieving, or caring.  It follows the ideas laid down by Professor Allan Kellehear in the Compassionate Cities Charter: Compassionate Cities Charter.
Examples of work carried out previously has revolved around arts and health approaches to health, supporting people dying alone in hospital, offering training to community organisations, and funding death cafés.
Pre-pandemic, NICE guidance suggested that around 30% of people that experience a close bereavement needed organised support opportunities.  Additionally, a further 10% struggled with complex or prolonged grief, needing specialist mental health interventions.  However, figures suggested at this time, 20-30% of bereaved adults were unable to access the support they needed.
Left unsupported, bereavement is associated with increased risk to health and wellbeing, including mortality, physical health problems, physical disability, medication usage, hospitalisation, and in some cases more visits to a GP.  The pre-pandemic costs of this were estimated to be £8bn annually plus an additional £23bn in lost revenue
The contract for the services will commence on 1st November 2026 and will be in place for a period of 3 years.

tender.title: Inclusive Growth (IG) Framework: Lot 7 Sustainability Services
tender.description:
London Legacy Development Corporation intends to establish the Inclusive Growth Framework, providing a flexible route to commission services that advance inclusive growth, equality, education, skills, employment, enterprise, community participation and evidence based decision making across Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, East London and the areas served by participating authorities. Framework is let for LLDC Group, wider GLA Group (OPDC, OSDC, LFB, MOPAC, MET, LONDON STADIUM), MDC's (LLDC, OSDC, OPDC) Local Boroughs,  East Bank Partners & QEOP Park Partners
This Notice is for: 
Lot 7: Sustainability Services
Suppliers appointed will be expected to provide sustainability support under the lens of the climate emergency response. These include services relating to the built environment; public realm; decarbonisation of our assets, transition to a 1.5 °C aligned future; risks and opportunities associated with climate adaptation and resilience; monitoring, reporting and accountability.
Typical services may include
Under the scope of our strategic priorities, typical services may include:
• Undertaking research and feasibility assessments to support decision making processes and business cases.
• Working with LLDC, GLAP and fellow mayoral functional bodies to create or update existing guidance, toolkits and pro-formas.
• Undertaking Climate Risk and Materiality Assessments and developing Adaptation Action Plans.
• Developing project specific case studies within a defined scope of works.
• Developing a methodology and undertaking natural capital carbon sequestration calculations and feasibility assessments.
• Discussing and collaborating on documents and data reviewed or meetings attended throughout the project’s lifetime.
• Reviewing documents and data to understand progress towards 1.5 °C requirements, providing technical analysis on performance and propose opportunities and measures for improvement.
• Review data collected to provide technical analysis and emerging trends.
• Discussing and collaborating on documents and data reviewed or meetings attended throughout a project’s lifetime.
• Updating on progress throughout, to allow the sustainability team to use existing lines of communication with colleagues to update them on progress.
• Providing continuous discussion and support when required.

tender.title: Pensions Actuarial Advisory Services Framework
tender.description:
National Grid is seeking to establish a multi-supplier framework agreement for the provision of Pensions Actuarial Advisory Services and related pensions, employee benefits, risk management, governance, and advisory support services across its UK pension arrangements. The framework will support both business-as-usual activities and project-based requirements and will be available for use by National Grid and its associated entities.
The framework is intended to provide access to suitably qualified suppliers capable of delivering specialist advice and support across a range of areas, including but not limited to:
Pensions actuarial and accounting advice.
Pension scheme funding and investment strategy support.
Governance and regulatory advisory services.
Pension benefit design and reward strategy.
Corporate transactions, mergers and acquisitions support.
Pension risk management and financial wellbeing advisory services.  
Employee benefits and related consultancy services.
National Grid intends to appoint up to nine (9) suppliers to the framework. The framework will operate through individual call-off engagements awarded either through direct award or mini-competition, depending on the nature of the requirement and the capabilities required. National Grid does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work under the framework.
The estimated value of the framework is £5.2 million over its full potential term, comprising an initial five (5) year term with the option to extend for up to three (3) additional one-year periods. Services will be supplied on an as-needed basis in accordance with the framework agreement and the requirements of individual call-off engagements.

procedure.features:
Initial Tender Submission
 Suppliers submit their technical and commercial responses by the tender deadline.
Evaluation
 National Grid will evaluate all submissions against the published technical and commercial award criteria.
Clarifications (if required)
 National Grid may request clarification on any aspect of a supplier's submission.
Negotiations (if required)
 National Grid may enter into negotiations with some or all suppliers and may reduce the number of suppliers progressing to the next stage.
Final Tender Submission (if required)
 Shortlisted suppliers may be invited to submit a revised or final tender.
Final Evaluation and Supplier Selection
 National Grid will complete the final evaluation and select the highest-ranking suppliers for appointment to the framework.
Award and Contract Execution
 Successful suppliers will be notified and the framework agreement will be executed following completion of any applicable standstill period.

frameworkAgreement.description:
The Framework Agreement will operate as a multi-supplier framework.
Call-off contracts may be awarded either by direct award or mini-competition. Direct awards may be used where a supplier has unique expertise, continuity is required, or urgent business or regulatory deadlines apply. Where multiple suppliers are capable of delivering the requirement, National Grid may conduct a mini-competition and evaluate proposals based on criteria such as technical approach, resources, experience, quality, and price.
Suppliers will submit framework hourly rates as part of this procurement. These rates may be used directly for call-off engagements, or National Grid may request project-specific pricing, fixed-fee proposals, or discounted rates through a mini-competition. Pricing may be negotiated to reflect the scope and complexity of individual requirements.
The Framework Agreement does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work, and services will be commissioned on an as-needed basis throughout the framework term.

milestones.description:
The Council intends to undertake preliminary market engagement in relation to the proposed procurement. The Council intends to contact relevant suppliers to invite expressions of interest and obtain information regarding supplier interest and market capacity.
The engagement will not form part of the subsequent tender evaluation and participation in the market engagement will not be a condition of participation in the subsequent procurement. The Council currently intends to conduct the subsequent procurement using the Open Procedure.
To submit an expression of interest please email procurement@royalgreenwich.gov.uk with the subject matter:
PME: EOI Metal Works 
stating that your company is a suitably qualified company to carry out these works and you would be interested in the upcoming tender.
Please note the upcoming tender will be an open tender published here on FTS and our e-procurement portal Proactis REGO. Therefore, there will not be any invitations sent out to suppliers who have expressed an interest. You will need to register an account on to the supplier e-procurement portal and look for alerts to when the tender is published.
